HUB.SUBTITLE: Guided tours that teach you LuxoInbox step by step, at your own pace.

WELCOME.TITLE: Welcome to LuxoInbox
WELCOME.BODY: Every message from every channel lands here, and this is where your team replies. Shall we walk you through the essentials?

FINISHED.TITLE: Tour completed
FINISHED.BODY: You now know this part of LuxoInbox. You can replay any tutorial whenever you like from the tutorial center.

GETTING_STARTED.NAME: First steps
GETTING_STARTED.DESCRIPTION: A quick map of the platform: the sidebar, search, your account and your profile.

WELCOME.TITLE: Welcome to LuxoInbox
WELCOME.BODY: This is your customer support hub: every message from every channel arrives here. Let's walk through the essentials in a few minutes.

INBOX.TITLE: Your notification inbox
INBOX.BODY: Mentions, assignments and alerts meant for you pile up here. Check it when you start your day so nothing slips through.

CONVERSATIONS.TITLE: Conversations
CONVERSATIONS.BODY: The heart of the product: every chat with a customer lives here. Expand the group to filter by folders, teams, channels or labels.

CONTACTS.TITLE: Contacts
CONTACTS.BODY: A profile for everyone who has written to you, with their details and history. Check it before replying so you have context.

REPORTS.TITLE: Reports
REPORTS.BODY: They measure conversation volume, response times and customer satisfaction. They help you decide with data instead of guesswork.

SEARCH.TITLE: Global search
SEARCH.BODY: Find conversations, contacts and messages from a single field. Open it with Cmd+K or Ctrl+K from any screen.

COMPOSE.TITLE: Start a conversation
COMPOSE.BODY: Here you write first: pick the channel, the recipient and the message. Perfect for following up with a customer.

ACCOUNT.TITLE: Your workspace account
ACCOUNT.BODY: If you belong to several accounts, switch between them from this selector. Each account has its own channels, agents and data.

SETTINGS.TITLE: Account settings
SETTINGS.BODY: Everything is configured from here: channels, agents, teams, automations and billing. This header tells you which section you are in.

PROFILE.TITLE: Your profile and preferences
PROFILE.BODY: Change your photo, availability, language and light or dark theme. You can also reopen this tutorial center from here.

NEXT.TITLE: That's the lay of the land
NEXT.BODY: You now have the general map. The next tour, Conversations, teaches you the day-to-day work.

CONVERSATIONS.NAME: Conversations
CONVERSATIONS.DESCRIPTION: How to read the inbox, open a chat, resolve it and use the contact panel.

LIST.TITLE: The conversation list
LIST.BODY: Each row is one conversation with a customer. The most recent rise to the top, and unread ones stand out.

TABS.TITLE: Filter by what is yours
TABS.BODY: Switch between conversations assigned to you, unassigned ones and everything in the account. Always start with yours.

CARD.TITLE: The card for each chat
CARD.BODY: It shows who is writing, through which channel, the last message and how long they have waited. Click to open the full conversation.

HEADER.TITLE: The conversation header
HEADER.BODY: Here you see the customer's name and assign the conversation to an agent or a team. Assigning stops two people answering the same thing.

RESOLVE.TITLE: Resolve or snooze
RESOLVE.BODY: Mark the conversation resolved once the customer is taken care of. If you are waiting on a reply, snooze it and it will come back on its own.

MORE_ACTIONS.TITLE: More actions
MORE_ACTIONS.BODY: Mute, email the transcript or mark as unread. These are occasional actions you will not need every day.

SIDEPANEL.TITLE: The contact panel
SIDEPANEL.BODY: On the right you get who the customer is, their details, labels and past conversations. Read it before you reply.

SIDEPANEL_SWITCH.TITLE: Switch panels
SIDEPANEL_SWITCH.BODY: Toggle between the contact details and the other panel views. You can hide it if you need more room to read.

LABELS.TITLE: Labels and priority
LABELS.BODY: Labels classify the conversation (sales, complaint, shipping) and priority says what to handle first. You set both from the right panel.

VIEWS.TITLE: Views and folders
VIEWS.BODY: Expand Conversations to reach mentions, unattended, teams, channels and labels. Folders save the filters you use most.

FINISH.TITLE: You know your way around
FINISH.BODY: You can find, open and close a conversation. The next tour teaches you how to write good replies.

REPLYING.NAME: Replying to messages
REPLYING.DESCRIPTION: The reply editor: private notes, attachments, shortcuts and canned responses.

COMPOSER.TITLE: The reply editor
COMPOSER.BODY: Anything you write here goes to the customer through the same channel they used. This is where you spend most of your day.

MODE.TITLE: Reply or private note
MODE.BODY: Switch between replying to the customer and leaving an internal note. Always check this toggle before you send.

PRIVATE_NOTE.TITLE: What a private note is for
PRIVATE_NOTE.BODY: Only your team sees a private note: use it to leave context, flag a delicate case or ask a teammate for help.

EDITOR.TITLE: Format your message
EDITOR.BODY: Use bold, lists, links and emoji so your reply reads better. Clear text means fewer follow-up questions.

SHORTCUTS.TITLE: Two shortcuts that save time
SHORTCUTS.BODY: Type / to insert a canned response, and {'@'} to mention a teammate inside a private note. Both open a menu right away.

ATTACHMENTS.TITLE: Attachments and extras
ATTACHMENTS.BODY: Send files, images, emoji or a voice note from this bar. Each channel has its own size and format limits.

SEND.TITLE: Send your reply
SEND.BODY: Send with the button or with Cmd+Enter. You can also schedule the message, or send and resolve in one step.

RESOLVE.TITLE: Close it when you are done
RESOLVE.BODY: After replying, resolve the conversation. That keeps your inbox honest and your reports clean.

CANNED.TITLE: Your canned responses
CANNED.BODY: Here you create the texts you reuse every day and give each one a short code. Then you insert them by typing / in the editor.

FINISH.TITLE: Ready to support
FINISH.BODY: You can reply, take notes and close. The next tour shows you how your customer information is stored.

CONTACTS.NAME: Contacts
CONTACTS.DESCRIPTION: Your customer database: profiles, segments, labels and attributes.

OVERVIEW.TITLE: Your customer base
OVERVIEW.BODY: Everyone who has ever written to you gets a profile here, with no manual work. Search by name, email or phone.

NAVIGATION.TITLE: Where contacts live
NAVIGATION.BODY: This menu group holds every contact view. Expand it to reach the segments and the labels.

ALL.TITLE: All contacts
ALL.BODY: The complete list, sorted by latest activity. It is your starting point when you look for someone specific.

SEGMENTS.TITLE: Saved segments
SEGMENTS.BODY: In the menu, under Contacts, you will find your segments: filters you save with a name, like customers in Bogota who wrote this month.

TAGS.TITLE: Contacts by label
TAGS.BODY: Right below it you can filter by the labels you put on people, such as VIP or overdue. It groups them without any manual lists.

CREATE.TITLE: Create a contact
CREATE.BODY: Add someone manually when you met them outside the chat. With an email or a phone number you can reach out first.

PROFILE.TITLE: What a profile holds
PROFILE.BODY: Basic details, company, location, the channels they write from and any custom attributes you define. All editable in one click.

HISTORY.TITLE: Notes and history
HISTORY.BODY: The profile shows past conversations and lets you leave internal notes. The next agent will not start from scratch.

ATTRIBUTES.TITLE: Custom attributes
ATTRIBUTES.BODY: Define the fields your business needs: policy number, plan, city. They will show up on every contact profile.

FINISH.TITLE: Your customers, organized
FINISH.BODY: You can search, create and enrich a profile. The next tour is for admins: how to connect channels.

INBOXES.NAME: Channels and inboxes
INBOXES.DESCRIPTION: Connect your website, WhatsApp or email and decide who staffs each channel.

CONCEPT.TITLE: What an inbox is
CONCEPT.BODY: An inbox is a connected channel: your website chat, a WhatsApp number, a mailbox. Each one has its own agents and rules.

NAVIGATION.TITLE: Where you manage them
NAVIGATION.BODY: Every inbox is created and configured from Settings. This is the entry point you will use whenever you add a channel.

LIST.TITLE: Your current inboxes
LIST.BODY: Here you see the channels already connected and their status. If a channel breaks, the alert shows up on this screen.

CHANNELS.TITLE: Pick the channel type
CHANNELS.BODY: This catalog holds everything you can connect: website, WhatsApp, email, social media and API. Pick one and follow the wizard.

WEBSITE.TITLE: Your website chat
WEBSITE.BODY: It is the quickest channel to launch: create the inbox and paste a code snippet into your site. Colors and greeting are customizable.

MESSAGING.TITLE: WhatsApp, email and social
MESSAGING.BODY: These channels ask you to authorize your account with the provider. Have the business credentials ready before starting the wizard.

MEMBERS.TITLE: Who staffs each channel
MEMBERS.BODY: Every inbox has its own agent list: only they see those conversations. Open it from the list and go to the members tab.

CONFIGURATION.TITLE: Key inbox settings
CONFIGURATION.BODY: Inside each inbox you set the automatic greeting, business hours, the satisfaction survey and the out-of-hours message.

AUTOMATION.TITLE: Automate the repetitive
AUTOMATION.BODY: Automations can label, assign or reply based on the incoming channel. They save minutes on every conversation.

FINISH.TITLE: Channels are ready
FINISH.BODY: You can connect and configure a channel. Now decide who works in them: take the Agents and teams tour.

TEAM.NAME: Agents and teams
TEAM.DESCRIPTION: Invite people, define their permissions and group them into working teams.

CONCEPT.TITLE: Agents, teams and roles
CONCEPT.BODY: An agent is a person who replies. A team groups agents by function, like Sales or Support. The role defines what each one can touch.

AGENTS.TITLE: The agent list
AGENTS.BODY: Here you see your whole team, their role and whether they accepted the invitation. You also deactivate whoever leaves.

INVITE.TITLE: Invite someone
INVITE.BODY: Type their email, choose the role and send. They get a link to set a password and sign in.

ROLES.TITLE: Administrator or agent
ROLES.BODY: An agent replies to conversations. An administrator also configures channels, teams and billing. Grant admin only to those who need it.

CUSTOM_ROLES.TITLE: Custom roles
CUSTOM_ROLES.BODY: If the two base roles fall short, build one with exact permissions: for example, view reports but never touch settings.

TEAMS.TITLE: Working teams
TEAMS.BODY: Group agents by specialty so you can assign conversations to all of them at once. An agent can belong to several teams.

TEAMS_PAGE.TITLE: Create and edit teams
TEAMS_PAGE.BODY: Give it a name, a description and pick its members. You can have them notified whenever something reaches the team.

ROUTING.TITLE: How teams get used
ROUTING.BODY: In a conversation you can assign a team instead of a person. It stays visible to all of them until someone picks it up.

AVAILABILITY.TITLE: Agent availability
AVAILABILITY.BODY: Everyone sets here whether they are online, busy or offline. Automatic routing only considers the people who are online.

FINISH.TITLE: Team is set up
FINISH.BODY: You can invite people, grant permissions and build teams. The next tour shows the tools that make the whole team faster.

PRODUCTIVITY.NAME: Productivity
PRODUCTIVITY.DESCRIPTION: Canned responses, macros, labels, automations and service level agreements.

CONCEPT.TITLE: Stop repeating yourself
CONCEPT.BODY: In customer support most cases look alike. These five tools turn that repetition into a single click.

CANNED.TITLE: Canned responses
CANNED.BODY: Texts you write once and reuse forever, each with a short code. Insert them by typing / in the conversation editor.

CANNED_PAGE.TITLE: Create your own
CANNED_PAGE.BODY: Give it a code that is easy to remember, like greeting or shipping, and write the message. The whole team can use it.

MACROS.TITLE: Macros: several actions at once
MACROS.BODY: A macro runs a sequence in one click: reply, label, assign and resolve. You trigger it from the conversation.

MACROS_USE.TITLE: When to use a macro
MACROS_USE.BODY: Use it for fixed processes: closing a complaint, escalating to billing or asking for details. If you do it three times a day, make it a macro.

LABELS.TITLE: Labels
LABELS.BODY: These are the categories you use to classify conversations and contacts. Keep them few and clear: nobody uses a huge list.

LABELS_USE.TITLE: What they are really for
LABELS_USE.BODY: Labels let you filter the inbox, measure in reports and trigger automations. They are the backbone of your data.

AUTOMATION.TITLE: Automations
AUTOMATION.BODY: Rules of the form when this happens, do that. They run on their own when a conversation arrives, changes or is resolved.

AUTOMATION_EXAMPLE.TITLE: A concrete example
AUTOMATION_EXAMPLE.BODY: If a message arrives on WhatsApp and mentions the word invoice, label it as billing and assign it to the Billing team.

SLA.TITLE: Service level agreements
SLA.BODY: They set how fast you promise to reply and resolve. When the deadline nears, the conversation is flagged so nobody forgets it.

FINISH.TITLE: Less manual work
FINISH.BODY: With these tools your team replies faster with the same quality. Come back to the center whenever you want to review them.

CAMPAIGNS.NAME: Campaigns
CAMPAIGNS.DESCRIPTION: Messages you send first: live chat, SMS and WhatsApp.

CONCEPT.TITLE: You make the first move
CONCEPT.BODY: A campaign is a message that starts on your side, not a reply. Use it to announce, remind or win customers back.

NAVIGATION.TITLE: Where campaigns live
NAVIGATION.BODY: This menu group holds the three available types. Each one has its own screen and its own rules.

PAGE.TITLE: The campaign list
PAGE.BODY: Here you see the campaigns you created, whether they are active and since when. You can pause or edit them any time.

LIVE_CHAT.TITLE: Live chat campaigns
LIVE_CHAT.BODY: These messages pop up on your website widget when someone visits a specific page. Great for catching interested visitors.

LIVE_CHAT_SETUP.TITLE: How you set it up
LIVE_CHAT_SETUP.BODY: Pick the website inbox, the page address, the text and the delay in seconds. Start with one message and measure it.

SMS.TITLE: SMS campaigns
SMS.BODY: Send a text message to a list of contacts on a set date. You need a connected SMS inbox.

WHATSAPP.TITLE: WhatsApp campaigns
WHATSAPP.BODY: They use templates approved by WhatsApp, so prepare those first. They get read the most, so use them wisely.

AUDIENCE.TITLE: Choosing the audience
AUDIENCE.BODY: The audience is built from your contact labels. Segment carefully: sending to everyone annoys people and hurts results.

METRICS.TITLE: Measuring the result
METRICS.BODY: After sending, check how many messages were delivered and how many conversations opened. That last number is the one that matters.

FINISH.TITLE: Campaigns are ready
FINISH.BODY: You can create, segment and measure. Remember that every reply to a campaign arrives as a normal conversation.

HELP_CENTER.NAME: Help center
HELP_CENTER.DESCRIPTION: Publish articles so customers can answer their own frequent questions.

CONCEPT.TITLE: Answer once, help many
CONCEPT.BODY: The help center is your public article site. Every frequent question you document is a conversation you will not have to handle.

NAVIGATION.TITLE: Where you edit it
NAVIGATION.BODY: All the content is written and published from this menu group. You do not need anyone from the technical team.

PAGE.TITLE: Your help portal
PAGE.BODY: A portal is a complete help site with its own name, language and address. You can have one per brand or per product.

PORTAL.TITLE: How it is organized
PORTAL.BODY: Portal, categories and articles: three levels. Think of categories as the chapters of a manual and articles as its pages.

ARTICLES.TITLE: Writing articles
ARTICLES.BODY: The editor takes headings, images, lists and links. Write the way you would talk to a customer, not like a technical manual.

CATEGORIES.TITLE: Categories
CATEGORIES.BODY: They group articles by topic so people find them fast. Five or six well-chosen categories are usually enough.

LOCALES.TITLE: Portal languages
LOCALES.BODY: You can publish the same portal in several languages. Each article is translated separately and keeps its category.

PUBLISH.TITLE: Draft and publish
PUBLISH.BODY: An article starts as a draft and only goes online when you publish it. Review it first: it is your brand's public voice.

DOMAIN.TITLE: Domain and appearance
DOMAIN.BODY: In the portal settings you set the logo, the colors and your own address. With a custom domain it looks like part of your website.

FINISH.TITLE: Help is published
FINISH.BODY: You can document and publish. Link articles from your replies: it saves time and the customer gets a better answer.

REPORTS.NAME: Reports
REPORTS.DESCRIPTION: Measure volume, response times, agent performance and satisfaction.

CONCEPT.TITLE: Deciding with data
CONCEPT.BODY: Reports answer three questions: how much work comes in, how fast we handle it and how happy the customer ends up.

NAVIGATION.TITLE: Where the reports live
NAVIGATION.BODY: This group holds every view. Each one answers a different question, so come in knowing what you want to find out.

OVERVIEW.TITLE: Overview
OVERVIEW.BODY: A summary of the current state: open conversations, unassigned ones and agents online. It is the picture right now.

LIVE.TITLE: What is happening today
LIVE.BODY: Live numbers help you react during the day: if the queue grows, add people or review how work is being assigned.

CONVERSATIONS.TITLE: Conversation report
CONVERSATIONS.BODY: Volume per day, first response and resolution time over the period you choose. Compare weeks to spot the trend.

AGENTS.TITLE: Performance by agent
AGENTS.BODY: How many conversations each person handled and how fast. Use it to balance workload, not to pressure people.

CSAT.TITLE: Customer satisfaction
CSAT.BODY: The survey sent when a conversation closes is summarized here. Read the comments: they are worth more than the average.

SLA.TITLE: SLA compliance
SLA.BODY: It shows what share of conversations met the deadlines you promised and which ones missed. Start with the breaches.

EXPORT.TITLE: Filter and export
EXPORT.BODY: Every report accepts a date range and filters. You can download them as CSV to analyze or share.

FINISH.TITLE: You know how to measure
FINISH.BODY: Check the reports once a week, not every day. Good decisions show up in the trend, not in the daily noise.

ASSIGNMENT.NAME: Automatic assignment
ASSIGNMENT.DESCRIPTION: Distribute conversations on their own, by capacity and available agents.

CONCEPT.TITLE: Let the system distribute
CONCEPT.BODY: Without automatic assignment someone has to hand out work. With it, each conversation reaches the right agent on its own.

NAVIGATION.TITLE: Where you configure it
NAVIGATION.BODY: Assignment policies live in Settings. You create them once and apply them to the inboxes you choose.

PAGE.TITLE: Your policies
PAGE.BODY: Here you see the policies you created and which inboxes they apply to. You can have several, one per channel or team.

POLICY.TITLE: What a policy is
POLICY.BODY: It is the rule that decides whose turn the next conversation is. It sets the distribution order and who is eligible.

CREATE.TITLE: Create a policy
CREATE.BODY: Give it a name, choose how work is shared and save. Then link it to one or more inboxes from each inbox's settings.

ORDER.TITLE: Distribution order
ORDER.BODY: Round robin shares evenly; balanced gives the conversation to whoever has the fewest open. If in doubt, start with round robin.

CAPACITY.TITLE: Capacity limits
CAPACITY.BODY: Set how many open conversations an agent can hold at once. Once at the cap they stop receiving until they close one.

INBOXES.TITLE: Linking the inboxes
INBOXES.BODY: A policy only acts on the inboxes where you enable it. Try it on a small channel before rolling it out everywhere.

AVAILABILITY.TITLE: Only agents who are online
AVAILABILITY.BODY: Automatic routing skips anyone who is offline. Remind your team to keep their status up to date.

FINISH.TITLE: Automatic routing is on
FINISH.BODY: No more handing out work by hand. Check the agent report in a few days to confirm the load came out even.

NAVIGATION.NAME: The sidebar
NAVIGATION.DESCRIPTION: A walk through the left-hand menu: where every section lives and how to get there fast.

INBOX.TITLE: My inbox
INBOX.BODY: Your personal alerts land here: mentions, conversations assigned to you and new messages. It is the first thing worth checking each morning.

CONVERSATIONS.TITLE: Conversations
CONVERSATIONS.BODY: This group opens every chat view: all, mentions, participating and unattended. It is where you will spend most of your day.

SUBGROUPS.TITLE: Folders, teams, channels and labels
SUBGROUPS.BODY: The group holds collapsible sub-groups. Channels lists your connected inboxes, Folders keeps your saved filters, and Teams and Labels group by owner and by topic.

CONTACTS.TITLE: Contacts
CONTACTS.BODY: Everyone who writes to you is stored here. Open a person to see their details and everything they discussed with you before, on any channel.

REPORTS.TITLE: Reports
REPORTS.BODY: Measure what happens: conversation volume, response times, load per agent and satisfaction. Only administrators and roles with report access see it.

SETTINGS.TITLE: Settings
SETTINGS.BODY: Everything that configures the account: agents, teams, inboxes, labels, automation and integrations. It unfolds in sections so nothing gets lost.

SETTINGS_SECTIONS.TITLE: The settings sections
SETTINGS_SECTIONS.BODY: Settings is grouped into blocks: workspace, productivity, AI, data and account. Account settings opens the general one: name, language and time zone.

SEARCH.TITLE: Search
SEARCH.BODY: Find messages, contacts, conversations and help-center articles from one place. It also answers to the keyboard shortcut, no mouse needed.

COMPOSE.TITLE: New conversation
COMPOSE.BODY: Reach out to a contact first, on the channel you choose. Handy for following up or reopening a case that was left hanging.

COLLAPSE.TITLE: Collapse the menu
COLLAPSE.BODY: Shrink the menu to a strip of icons and gain width for reading messages. Click it again whenever you want the names back.

SEARCH_AND_COMMANDS.NAME: Search and commands
SEARCH_AND_COMMANDS.DESCRIPTION: Find any message or contact and run actions without lifting your hands off the keyboard.

ENTRY.TITLE: The global search
ENTRY.BODY: Opens search across the whole account. It looks through messages, contacts, conversations and help-center articles at the same time.

WHAT_IT_FINDS.TITLE: What you can search for
WHAT_IT_FINDS.BODY: Type a name, an email, a phone number or a conversation id. It also works with the exact wording of a message you remember.

TABS.TITLE: Results by type
TABS.BODY: The tabs split Conversations, Messages, Contacts and Articles. Start on the right tab and you will skip results that were never going to help.

FILTERS.TITLE: Narrow it down
FILTERS.BODY: You can limit results by sender, by inbox and by date range. That is how hundreds of matches become the five that matter.

TIPS.TITLE: Tricks that save time
TIPS.BODY: Searching by conversation id, email or phone number is far more precise than searching by name. Your recent searches stay listed below the field.

COMMAND_BAR.TITLE: The command bar
COMMAND_BAR.BODY: Press Cmd+K or Ctrl+K on any screen, type what you want to do and run it: jump to a section, change a chat status or fire a macro.

SHORTCUTS.TITLE: Keyboard shortcuts
SHORTCUTS.BODY: This entry opens the full shortcut list. The ones you will use most: resolve, open the next conversation and switch between reply and private note.

FINISH.TITLE: You search like a pro now
FINISH.BODY: With search and the command bar you reach anywhere in two seconds. This is the habit that will save you the most time.

PROFILE_AND_PREFERENCES.NAME: Your profile
PROFILE_AND_PREFERENCES.DESCRIPTION: Set up your picture, signature, language, availability and account security.

PROFILE.TITLE: Profile settings
PROFILE.BODY: Change your picture, display name, email and password here. The display name is what your teammates see inside the dashboard.

INTERFACE.TITLE: Interface
INTERFACE.BODY: The Interface section is where you pick your preferred language and the dashboard font size. The language is yours alone; it does not affect teammates.

SIGNATURE.TITLE: Personal message signature
SIGNATURE.BODY: Write a signature and it gets appended to every message you send. It works on live-chat, email and API inboxes.

SEND_KEY.TITLE: Send-message hotkey
SEND_KEY.BODY: Choose whether you send with Enter or with Cmd/Ctrl+Enter. If you tend to write long replies, Cmd/Ctrl+Enter stops you sending them half-finished.

NOTIFICATIONS.TITLE: Notification preferences
NOTIFICATIONS.BODY: Decide what reaches you by email and what by push: conversation assigned, mention, new message or a missed SLA.

AVAILABILITY.TITLE: Your availability
AVAILABILITY.BODY: Set yourself online, busy or offline. Auto-assignment only hands conversations to agents who are online.

AUTO_OFFLINE.TITLE: Auto-offline
AUTO_OFFLINE.BODY: Turn this on and the system marks you offline when you stop using the dashboard. That way you are not assigned chats nobody will answer.

APPEARANCE.TITLE: Appearance
APPEARANCE.BODY: Switch between light, dark or the system theme. If you work long stretches, dark is easier on the eyes.

MFA.TITLE: Two-step verification
MFA.BODY: Under Two-Factor Authentication you enable a time-based code from your authenticator app. Keep the backup codes somewhere safe.

FINISH.TITLE: Your account, your way
FINISH.BODY: Profile, signature, language and security are set. Check your availability every morning and the workload will route itself.

NOTIFICATIONS_INBOX.NAME: My inbox
NOTIFICATIONS_INBOX.DESCRIPTION: Your personal alert list: what lands there, how to read it and how to empty it daily.

ENTRY.TITLE: My inbox
ENTRY.BODY: This is your personal alert list, separate from the conversation list. Only what concerns you shows up here.

WHAT_ARRIVES.TITLE: What lands here
WHAT_ARRIVES.BODY: Conversations assigned to you, mentions in private notes, new messages on chats you follow and missed-SLA alerts.

READING.TITLE: Reading an alert
READING.BODY: Opening an alert shows the whole conversation beside it, so you can reply without leaving the inbox. It is marked as read on open.

DISPLAY.TITLE: The Display menu
DISPLAY.BODY: Sort by newest, oldest or priority, and choose whether snoozed items, read items and labels stay visible.

ACTIONS.TITLE: Actions on an alert
ACTIONS.BODY: Mark as read or unread, snooze or delete. You can also mark everything as read and clear the inbox in one go.

SNOOZE.TITLE: Snoozing an alert
SNOOZE.BODY: If you cannot handle it now, snooze it and it comes back when you said. Far better than leaving it unread and forgetting it.

DIFFERENCE.TITLE: Not the same as Conversations
DIFFERENCE.BODY: The inbox is your alerts; Conversations is the team's workload. Empty the inbox daily, but work the rest of your shift from the conversation views.

FINISH.TITLE: Inbox under control
FINISH.BODY: Start the day in the inbox so nothing is left hanging, then run the rest of your shift from your conversation views.

ACCOUNTS.NAME: Accounts
ACCOUNTS.DESCRIPTION: What an account is, how to switch between several and what carries over between them.

CURRENT.TITLE: The active account
CURRENT.BODY: The top of the menu shows the account you are working in. Everything on screen belongs to that account and nothing else.

SWITCH.TITLE: Switching accounts
SWITCH.BODY: If you belong to several, pick one here and the dashboard reloads with its conversations, contacts and reports. Your role is shown next to each.

ISOLATION.TITLE: Each account stands alone
ISOLATION.BODY: Conversations, contacts, inboxes, labels and reports never mix across accounts. What you do in one never shows up in another.

ROLES.TITLE: Your role changes per account
ROLES.BODY: You can be an administrator in one account and an agent in another. That is why the sidebar does not always show the same sections.

SHARED_PROFILE.TITLE: Your profile is shared
SHARED_PROFILE.BODY: Picture, name, email and password are yours and travel with you. Availability and notifications, though, are set per account.

FINISH.TITLE: Always know where you are
FINISH.BODY: Confirm the active account before you reply. It is the most common slip when you work several brands at once.

CONVERSATION_VIEWS.NAME: Conversation views
CONVERSATION_VIEWS.DESCRIPTION: All, mentions, participating and unattended, plus the folder, team, channel and label sub-groups.

GROUP.TITLE: The Conversations group
GROUP.BODY: It gathers every way of looking at the same workload. Switching views does not change the data, only the slice you see.

ALL.TITLE: All conversations
ALL.BODY: The full account view, limited to what your role is allowed to see. Use it for the big picture, not for day-to-day work.

MENTIONS.TITLE: Mentions
MENTIONS.BODY: Only the conversations where a teammate named you in a private note. These are usually requests for help, so check them early.

PARTICIPATING.TITLE: Participating
PARTICIPATING.BODY: Conversations you took part in even though they are not yours. Handy for following a case you handed over to someone else.

UNATTENDED.TITLE: Unattended
UNATTENDED.BODY: Chats with customer messages that nobody on the team has answered yet. This is the view that stops someone being left waiting.

FOLDERS.TITLE: Folders
FOLDERS.BODY: Every folder is a saved filter with a name. Create one for what you check daily and it is always a single click away.

TEAMS.TITLE: Teams
TEAMS.BODY: Groups conversations by the team they are assigned to: sales, support, billing. Useful when you are covering for a colleague.

CHANNELS.TITLE: Channels
CHANNELS.BODY: One inbox per connected channel: web, WhatsApp, email, social. Come in this way when you want to work a single channel.

LABELS.TITLE: Labels
LABELS.BODY: Filter by the topic you gave the conversation: complaint, shipping, refund. Labels are applied from the right-hand panel.

FINISH.TITLE: Pick the right view
FINISH.BODY: Start with Unattended and what is assigned to you, and keep All for the overview. Working by views is what stops duplicated replies.

CONVERSATION_FILTERS.NAME: Filtering conversations
CONVERSATION_FILTERS.DESCRIPTION: Status and assignee tabs, sorting, advanced filters and how to save them as a folder.

STATUS.TITLE: Filter by status
STATUS.BODY: Open, Resolved, Pending, Snoozed or All. Work from Open and keep the rest for reviewing or auditing.

ASSIGNEE.TITLE: Mine, Unassigned and All
ASSIGNEE.BODY: Mine are your conversations, Unassigned the ones nobody picked up and All the whole account. Start with yours, then help with the free ones.

SORT.TITLE: Sorting the list
SORT.BODY: Sort by last activity, creation date, priority or waiting time. Sorting by waiting time is the surest way to leave nobody hanging.

ADVANCED.TITLE: Filter conversations
ADVANCED.BODY: Opens the advanced filter panel so you can combine conditions: channel, agent, team, label, status, priority or contact attributes.

PANEL.TITLE: Build your filter
PANEL.BODY: Add one condition per line and join them with the and/or selectors. When it is ready, hit Apply filters and the list narrows instantly.

SAVE.TITLE: Save filter
SAVE.BODY: If a filter earns its keep every day, save it with a name and it becomes a folder inside the Conversations group.

RESET.TITLE: Clear filters
RESET.BODY: Puts the list back to normal. Reach for it whenever conversations you know exist have stopped showing up.

FOLDERS.TITLE: Your folders in the menu
FOLDERS.BODY: Saved filters appear here as Folders, one click away. You can edit or delete them from the same list header.

FINISH.TITLE: The list, on your terms
FINISH.BODY: Status, assignee, sorting and advanced filters all stack. Save the two or three you use daily and never rebuild them again.

BULK_ACTIONS.NAME: Bulk actions
BULK_ACTIONS.DESCRIPTION: Select several conversations and assign, label or close them all in one move.

WHERE.TITLE: Working in batches
WHERE.BODY: When the list piles up, do not open it one row at a time. You can select several conversations and apply the same action at once.

SELECT.TITLE: The selection checkbox
SELECT.BODY: Tick a conversation's checkbox to select it. In the compact view it appears when you hover over the contact's picture.

BAR.TITLE: The bulk action bar
BAR.BODY: Selecting brings up this bar with the count and everything you can do with those conversations. Clear undoes the selection.

AGENT.TITLE: Assign an agent
AGENT.BODY: Spread the batch across the team, or remove the agent to send them back to Unassigned.

TEAM.TITLE: Assign a team
TEAM.BODY: Hand the batch to the right team: sales, support, billing. Each team then distributes them internally.

LABEL.TITLE: Add or remove labels
LABEL.BODY: Classify many conversations with the same topic in one step, or strip off a label that no longer applies.

STATUS.TITLE: Change status
STATUS.BODY: Resolve, reopen or snooze the whole batch. It is the fastest way to close out a run you have already handled.

SELECT_ALL.TITLE: Select the whole page
SELECT_ALL.BODY: Ticks every conversation currently visible. Pair it with a filter to act on one specific group.

SCOPE.TITLE: Only the page you see
SCOPE.BODY: The selection covers just the conversations loaded on screen, not the whole account. Scroll down and select again if you need more.

FINISH.TITLE: Close batches in seconds
FINISH.BODY: Filter, select, apply. With that habit a list of fifty conversations gets tidied in a minute.

CONVERSATION_ACTIONS.NAME: Closing conversations
CONVERSATION_ACTIONS.DESCRIPTION: Resolve, snooze, mark as pending and the rest of the actions in the chat header.

HEADER.TITLE: The chat header
HEADER.BODY: It gathers everything you can do with the open conversation: close it, snooze it, call, or check the times you committed to.

RESOLVE.TITLE: Resolve
RESOLVE.BODY: Marks the conversation as handled and takes it out of the open list. If the customer writes again, it reopens on its own.

MORE.TITLE: The resolve dropdown
MORE.BODY: The arrow next to the button opens the ways of closing that are not a final close: snooze and mark as pending.

SNOOZE.TITLE: Snooze
SNOOZE.BODY: Pick how long: until the next reply, tomorrow or next week. The conversation leaves your list and comes back by itself.

PENDING.TITLE: Mark as pending
PENDING.BODY: Use it when you have replied but the case is still open on your side: a shipment, a refund, an approval. It does not count as resolved.

OTHER.TITLE: More actions
OTHER.BODY: The three-dot menu adds muting the contact, emailing the transcript and marking the conversation as unread.

SLA.TITLE: The conversation SLA
SLA.BODY: Shows the time committed for the first response, the next response and the resolution. Red means the target is already missed.

CALL.TITLE: Call the contact
CALL.BODY: Where the channel supports it, start a call from inside the conversation. The call is logged in the contact's history.

ASSIGN.TITLE: Assign and prioritise
ASSIGN.BODY: Conversation actions on the right panel is where you set agent, team, priority and labels. Assigning stops two people answering the same chat.

FINISH.TITLE: Every chat gets an ending
FINISH.BODY: Resolved, snoozed or pending: no conversation should sit open without a reason. Your reports and your team will thank you.

CONTACT_PANEL.NAME: The contact panel
CONTACT_PANEL.DESCRIPTION: Everything you know about the customer while you reply: details, history, attributes, notes and files.

PANEL.TITLE: The right-hand panel
PANEL.BODY: It backs every conversation with the customer's context. You can drag its sections around to keep the one you check most at the top.

SWITCH.TITLE: Contact or Copilot
SWITCH.BODY: Toggle between the contact record and the AI assistant. You can also hide the panel and gain width for reading messages.

INFO.TITLE: Contact details
INFO.BODY: Name, picture, email, phone and the channel they write from. From here you can open their full record if you need to edit it.

ACTIONS.TITLE: Conversation actions
ACTIONS.BODY: Assign agent and team, set the priority and apply labels. This is the block you will use most in the whole panel.

PARTICIPANTS.TITLE: Participants
PARTICIPANTS.BODY: The teammates following this conversation. They are notified of every new message even when they are not the assigned agent.

CONVERSATION_INFO.TITLE: Conversation information
CONVERSATION_INFO.BODY: Technical details about the contact: browser, system, location and the page they wrote from. It helps you reproduce a problem.

ATTRIBUTES.TITLE: Contact attributes
ATTRIBUTES.BODY: The fields your business defines: plan, customer number, city. An administrator creates them and you fill them in here.

PREVIOUS.TITLE: Previous conversations
PREVIOUS.BODY: Everything this customer discussed with you before, on any channel. Read it first and you will not ask for what they already told you.

NOTES.TITLE: Contact notes
NOTES.BODY: Lasting notes about the person, not about one chat. Ideal for agreements, preferences or warnings about the case.

FILES.TITLE: Attachments
FILES.BODY: Collects the images and files exchanged in the conversation. Download them from here or jump straight to the original message.

COMPOSER_ADVANCED.NAME: The editor in depth
COMPOSER_ADVANCED.DESCRIPTION: Emojis, attachments, voice notes, signature, templates and the shortcuts that speed up every reply.

TOOLBAR.TITLE: The editor toolbar
TOOLBAR.BODY: Below the writing area sits everything you can add to a message. The buttons change with the channel the customer writes from.

EMOJI.TITLE: Emojis
EMOJI.BODY: Opens the picker so you can add an emoji without leaving the keyboard. Used sparingly, they make a message sound warmer.

ATTACHMENTS.TITLE: Attach files
ATTACHMENTS.BODY: Upload images, PDFs or documents, or drag them onto the editor. Each channel has its own size and format limits.

AUDIO.TITLE: Record a voice note
AUDIO.BODY: Record a voice note from the panel and send it as a message. Useful for long explanations on the channels that allow it.

SIGNATURE.TITLE: Message signature
SIGNATURE.BODY: Turn your personal signature on or off for this message only. The signature text itself lives in your profile settings.

QUOTE.TITLE: Quoted thread
QUOTE.BODY: On email, decide whether the previous thread is included below your reply. Without it the message reads much cleaner.

WA_TEMPLATE.TITLE: WhatsApp templates
WA_TEMPLATE.BODY: After 24 hours without a customer reply, WhatsApp only lets you write using an approved template. This is where you pick one.

ARTICLE.TITLE: Insert an article
ARTICLE.BODY: Search the help center and drop an article into your reply as a link. You resolve faster and the customer keeps the guide.

SHORTCUTS.TITLE: Three shortcuts inside the text
SHORTCUTS.BODY: Type / to insert a canned response and {'@'} to mention a teammate in a private note. Variables in double curly braces pull in customer data.

SEND.TITLE: Send
SEND.BODY: Send with the button or with your hotkey. You can also schedule the message or send and resolve the conversation in one step.

COPILOT.NAME: Copilot
COPILOT.DESCRIPTION: The AI assistant that summarises the conversation and drafts your reply.

WHERE.TITLE: Where Copilot lives
WHERE.BODY: In the right-hand panel switch, next to the contact record. Copilot stays inside the conversation, so you never change screen.

PANEL.TITLE: The Copilot panel
PANEL.BODY: It reads the open conversation and answers in whatever language you write to it. If you are unsure where to start, use the suggested prompts.

ASK.TITLE: What to ask it
ASK.BODY: A summary of the case, a draft reply, a change of tone or a translation of the last message. The more specific the ask, the better the answer.

SOURCES.TITLE: Where its answers come from
SOURCES.BODY: It draws on the open conversation and on the account's AI assistant knowledge: its documents and its FAQs.

INSERT.TITLE: Move the reply to the editor
INSERT.BODY: Copy the draft into the editor, read it and adjust it before sending. Copilot proposes; the reply that goes out is still yours.

LAUNCHER.TITLE: Copilot outside a chat
LAUNCHER.BODY: Away from a conversation, this floating button opens Copilot on any screen for general questions.

FINISH.TITLE: One more teammate
FINISH.BODY: Use it to start the reply, not to send it blind. Always reviewing the draft is what keeps the quality up.

CONTACTS_SEARCH_SEGMENTS.NAME: Search and segments
CONTACTS_SEARCH_SEGMENTS.DESCRIPTION: Find contacts with search and filters, and save the lists you keep rebuilding as segments.

SEARCH.TITLE: Search for a contact
SEARCH.BODY: Type a name, an email or a phone number and the list narrows as you type. This is the fastest route when you know who you want.

FILTER.TITLE: Filter by what you need
FILTER.BODY: This button opens the Filter contacts panel. Use it to build lists by country, city, company, last activity or any custom attribute.

CONDITIONS.TITLE: Stack several conditions
CONDITIONS.BODY: Stack conditions with Add filter and run them with Apply filters. While filters are active, a save icon appears next to the button.

SAVE_SEGMENT.TITLE: Save the filter as a segment
SAVE_SEGMENT.BODY: Give it a name and the whole team can use it. A segment recalculates itself: it always shows the contacts that match those conditions.

SEGMENTS_LIST.TITLE: Your saved segments
SEGMENTS_LIST.BODY: Inside Contacts in the sidebar, the Segments group lists everything you saved. One click brings that filtered list straight back.

TAGGED_WITH.TITLE: Tagged with
TAGGED_WITH.BODY: Every label you use on contacts shows up here. It is the shortcut for pulling up, say, all the customers marked as wholesale.

ACTIVE.TITLE: Active contacts
ACTIVE.BODY: The Active link shows who is browsing your site right now. Use it to offer help at the moment it still counts.

DELETE_SEGMENT.TITLE: Edit or delete a segment
DELETE_SEGMENT.BODY: Open the segment and use the pencil to change its conditions or the bin to remove it. Deleting a segment never deletes contacts.

FINISH.TITLE: You can segment on your own
FINISH.BODY: Save the searches you repeat every week and your working lists will always be one click away.

CONTACT_DETAIL.NAME: Contact profile
CONTACT_DETAIL.DESCRIPTION: Everything you know about a person: details, attributes, history, notes, files and duplicate merges.

FROM_LIST.TITLE: Open it from the list
FROM_LIST.BODY: Go to All Contacts and click a row. The full profile opens without losing the place you were working in.

PROFILE.TITLE: The contact profile
PROFILE.BODY: The left side holds their details: name, email, phone, company, city and social links. It is the team's source of truth.

EDIT.TITLE: Edit and block
EDIT.BODY: Change any field from Edit contact details and upload an avatar. If you need to, Block contact stops their messages coming in.

TABS.TITLE: The panel on the right
TABS.BODY: It has five tabs: Attributes, History, Notes, Media and Merge. Each one adds context that saves you asking the same thing twice.

ATTRIBUTES.TITLE: Attributes
ATTRIBUTES.BODY: The fields your business cares about: plan, customer number, delivery city. You define them in Settings and fill them in here.

HISTORY.TITLE: History
HISTORY.BODY: Every earlier conversation this person had, with any agent and on any channel. Read it before replying so you do not repeat questions.

NOTES_MEDIA.TITLE: Notes and Media
NOTES_MEDIA.BODY: Notes holds internal remarks the customer never sees. Media collects the files and images they shared with you.

MERGE.TITLE: Merge duplicates
MERGE.BODY: If the same person wrote from two channels, Merge folds both records into one. Pick the primary contact: its attributes win.

FINISH.TITLE: You know the profile now
FINISH.BODY: Keep these details current and every conversation starts with context instead of questions.

CONTACTS_BULK_IMPORT.NAME: Bulk actions
CONTACTS_BULK_IMPORT.DESCRIPTION: Label or delete many contacts at once and bring your database in from CSV or another tool.

WHY.TITLE: Work in batches
WHY.BODY: Once you have hundreds of contacts, touching them one by one does not scale. The list lets you select several and act on all of them.

SELECT.TITLE: Select contacts
SELECT.BODY: Hover a contact's avatar and a checkbox appears in its place. Tick the rows you want and an action bar opens above the list.

BULK_BAR.TITLE: The action bar
BULK_BAR.BODY: It shows up above the list as soon as something is selected: it counts your picks, takes the whole page, and holds the actions.

LABELS.TITLE: Label in bulk
LABELS.BODY: Assign labels adds them to everything selected and Remove labels does the opposite. That is how you prep segments or campaigns fast.

CSV.TITLE: Import contacts from CSV
CSV.BODY: The actions menu in the header has Import contacts: download the sample csv, keep its columns and upload your file.

DATA_PAGE.TITLE: Data: imports
DATA_PAGE.BODY: In Settings, the Data section brings contacts and conversations over from another support tool. Each import runs in the background.

DATA_NEW.TITLE: New import
DATA_NEW.BODY: Pick the source, paste its access key and choose which data to bring. You get live progress and a CSV of everything skipped.

FINISH.TITLE: Your database is in
FINISH.BODY: Between imports and bulk actions you can switch tools without losing history or labels.

COMPANIES.NAME: Companies
COMPANIES.DESCRIPTION: Group contacts by company and review its profile, its people, its history and its notes.

CONCEPT.TITLE: What a company is
CONCEPT.BODY: A company groups several contacts from the same organisation. It lets you support whole accounts instead of scattered people.

NAVIGATION.TITLE: Where companies live
NAVIGATION.BODY: Companies is its own sidebar entry, right next to Contacts. From there you see every company in the account.

LIST.TITLE: The company list
LIST.BODY: Each row shows the name, the domain, how many contacts it holds and its last activity. Click one to open its profile.

SEARCH_SORT.TITLE: Search and sort
SEARCH_SORT.BODY: Search by name in the field at the top and use Sort by to order them by domain, contact count or last activity.

CREATE.TITLE: Add company
CREATE.BODY: Add company registers a new one; a name and a domain are enough. The domain helps link contacts to it automatically.

DETAIL.TITLE: The company profile
DETAIL.BODY: Opening it shows the profile on the left and four tabs on the right: Attributes, Contacts, History and Notes.

CONTACTS.TITLE: Its people
CONTACTS.BODY: In Contacts you attach existing people with Link contact, or remove them from the company when they change jobs.

HISTORY_NOTES.TITLE: History and Notes
HISTORY_NOTES.BODY: History gathers the conversations of all its contacts, and Notes keeps the agreements and internal context of the account.

FINISH.TITLE: Accounts under control
FINISH.BODY: With companies up to date you can tell at a glance who you are talking to and what happened before with that account.

INBOX_WEBSITE.NAME: Website live chat
INBOX_WEBSITE.DESCRIPTION: Create the Website inbox, configure its widget and paste the snippet into your page.

CONCEPT.TITLE: What an inbox is
CONCEPT.BODY: An inbox is a connected channel: a website, a WhatsApp number, a mailbox. Everything arriving through it lands in your conversations.

NAVIGATION.TITLE: Settings, Inboxes
NAVIGATION.BODY: Open Settings in the sidebar and go to Inboxes. That is where you see the ones you have and create new ones.

CHANNELS.TITLE: Choose Channel
CHANNELS.BODY: This grid lists every channel you can connect. Each card opens its own setup form.

CARD.TITLE: Website
CARD.BODY: This is the live chat your visitors will see. No third-party account needed: LuxoInbox builds the widget for you.

FORM.TITLE: Configure the widget
FORM.BODY: Set the inbox name, the website domain and the welcome heading. This is exactly what a visitor sees on your page.

GREETING.TITLE: Greeting and reply time
GREETING.BODY: Turn on Enable channel greeting to send an automatic hello, and pick the reply time the chat will display.

AGENTS.TITLE: Add agents
AGENTS.BODY: The next step asks who will handle this inbox. Only those agents see its conversations, and you can change the list any time.

SCRIPT.TITLE: Copy the snippet
SCRIPT.BODY: The last screen shows a script. Paste it at the end of your site's body and the chat starts working.

FINISH.TITLE: Your chat is live
FINISH.BODY: Try the widget on your own site: the conversation should show up in your list within seconds.

INBOX_WHATSAPP.NAME: Connect WhatsApp
INBOX_WHATSAPP.DESCRIPTION: Choose between WhatsApp Cloud, Twilio or the QR code and start answering your number in LuxoInbox.

CONCEPT.TITLE: WhatsApp as a channel
CONCEPT.BODY: You connect a number and its messages arrive as normal conversations. You can run several numbers, each with its own inbox.

CARD.TITLE: The WhatsApp card
CARD.BODY: From Choose Channel, open WhatsApp. The next decision is which provider your number connects through.

PROVIDERS.TITLE: Pick your provider
PROVIDERS.BODY: This is where you decide how the number connects. The right option depends on whether you already have WhatsApp Business API access.

CLOUD.TITLE: WhatsApp Cloud
CLOUD.BODY: The official Meta route. It asks for the phone number ID, the business account ID and the API key from the developer console.

EMBEDDED.TITLE: Quick setup with Meta
EMBEDDED.BODY: Where available, it sends you to sign in with Meta and configures the number and webhooks for you. Have admin access ready.

TWILIO.TITLE: Twilio
TWILIO.BODY: If you already use Twilio, connect with your Account SID and Auth Token. The number must be WhatsApp-enabled in Twilio.

EVOLUTION.TITLE: WhatsApp QR
EVOLUTION.BODY: The quickest route: generate a QR code and scan it from Linked Devices on your phone. No API account required.

MIGRATION.TITLE: Move an existing number
MIGRATION.BODY: If your number already lives on another platform, the manual migration walks you through moving it without losing its verification.

FINISH.TITLE: WhatsApp connected
FINISH.BODY: Send a test message to that number: a new conversation should open in your list.

INBOX_SOCIAL.NAME: Social channels
INBOX_SOCIAL.DESCRIPTION: Connect Facebook, Instagram and TikTok so their messages land in one place.

CONCEPT.TITLE: Messages from social
CONCEPT.BODY: Each network connects as another inbox. Its direct messages arrive in your list alongside WhatsApp and website chats.

CHANNELS.TITLE: Choose Channel
CHANNELS.BODY: The social cards live in this grid. Only the ones enabled on your installation are shown.

FACEBOOK.TITLE: Facebook
FACEBOOK.BODY: Connect a Facebook page. Choosing it asks you to sign in and authorise access to that page's messages.

FACEBOOK_SETUP.TITLE: Pick the page
FACEBOOK_SETUP.BODY: After authorising, select the page from the dropdown and name the inbox. You need to be an admin of that page.

INSTAGRAM.TITLE: Instagram
INSTAGRAM.BODY: Connect a professional Instagram account to receive its direct messages. The account must allow message access.

TIKTOK.TITLE: TikTok
TIKTOK.BODY: Connect your TikTok account to handle the messages that arrive there. It only appears if your installation has the app configured.

PERMISSIONS.TITLE: Permissions and ownership
PERMISSIONS.BODY: All of these connections rely on permissions you grant inside the network. Always connect with the account that owns the profile.

REAUTHORIZE.TITLE: Reconnect when it expires
REAUTHORIZE.BODY: If the authorisation lapses, the inbox shows a notice to reconnect it. Do it quickly: no messages come in meanwhile.

FINISH.TITLE: Social in one inbox
FINISH.BODY: With the networks connected you stop hopping between apps and answer everything from the same list.

INBOX_EMAIL.NAME: Email channel
INBOX_EMAIL.DESCRIPTION: Receive and answer email in LuxoInbox using Google, Microsoft, forwarding or IMAP and SMTP.

CONCEPT.TITLE: Email as a channel
CONCEPT.BODY: Every incoming email becomes a conversation and your replies go out as email. The customer never notices the difference.

NAVIGATION.TITLE: Settings, Inboxes
NAVIGATION.BODY: Open Settings in the sidebar and go to Inboxes to create the email channel.

CHANNELS.TITLE: Choose Channel
CHANNELS.BODY: Look for the email card in the channel grid. From there you choose how your mailbox connects.

CARD.TITLE: Email
CARD.BODY: This is the inbox for your support mailbox: the address you publish on your site, your invoices or your signature.

PROVIDERS.TITLE: Three ways to connect
PROVIDERS.BODY: You can use Google, Microsoft or Other providers. The first two authorise in one click; the third asks for the details by hand.

OAUTH.TITLE: Google or Microsoft
OAUTH.BODY: Sign in with the mailbox account and authorise access. Sending and receiving are configured without handling any password.

OTHER_PROVIDERS.TITLE: IMAP and SMTP
OTHER_PROVIDERS.BODY: With Other providers you enter server, port and credentials: IMAP to receive and SMTP to send. Without both, mail does not flow.

FORWARDING.TITLE: Forwarding address
FORWARDING.BODY: When you finish you get a LuxoInbox address. Set your mailbox to forward there and everything lands in this inbox.

FINISH.TITLE: Email connected
FINISH.BODY: Send yourself a test email to the mailbox: within a minute it should turn up as a conversation.

INBOX_MESSAGING.NAME: SMS, Telegram and API
INBOX_MESSAGING.DESCRIPTION: Connect messaging channels such as SMS, Telegram and Line, or build your own with the API channel.

CONCEPT.TITLE: Other messaging channels
CONCEPT.BODY: Beyond website chat and WhatsApp you can connect SMS, Telegram, Line, or your own system through the API channel.

CHANNELS.TITLE: Choose Channel
CHANNELS.BODY: All of these live in the same grid. The form changes with the provider, but the flow is always identical.

SMS.TITLE: SMS
SMS.BODY: Handle text messages from a number of your own. Useful for notifications and for customers with no mobile data.

SMS_PROVIDERS.TITLE: Twilio or Bandwidth
SMS_PROVIDERS.BODY: SMS connects through Twilio or Bandwidth. You need their credentials and a number already purchased in their console.

TELEGRAM.TITLE: Telegram
TELEGRAM.BODY: Create a bot with BotFather inside Telegram, copy its Bot Token and paste it here. The channel is live in a minute.

LINE.TITLE: Line
LINE.BODY: It asks for the LINE channel ID, secret and token, which you get from the LINE developers console.

API.TITLE: API channel
API.BODY: For connecting a system of your own: you push messages through the API and receive the events on your webhook URL.

CALLBACKS.TITLE: Callback URL
CALLBACKS.BODY: Several of these channels show a URL at the end. Paste it into the provider's console or the messages will never arrive.

FINISH.TITLE: More channels, one inbox
FINISH.BODY: It does not matter where the customer writes from: everything ends up in the same conversation list.

INBOX_VOICE.NAME: Voice calls
INBOX_VOICE.DESCRIPTION: Create the Voice channel with Twilio and turn on calling for your WhatsApp number.

CONCEPT.TITLE: Talking, not just typing
CONCEPT.BODY: The voice channel lets you take calls inside LuxoInbox, with the contact's profile in view while you talk.

CHANNELS.TITLE: Choose Channel
CHANNELS.BODY: The voice cards sit at the end of the channel grid, next to the messaging ones.

VOICE_CARD.TITLE: Voice
VOICE_CARD.BODY: Connect a Twilio number to take phone calls. The number has to be purchased in your Twilio account first.

CREDENTIALS.TITLE: Twilio credentials
CREDENTIALS.BODY: The form asks for Account SID, Auth Token, API Key SID and API Key Secret, plus the number in international format.

TWILIO_URLS.TITLE: Configure Twilio
TWILIO_URLS.BODY: At the end you get the Twilio Voice URL and the status callback URL. Paste both into your Twilio number or no calls arrive.

WHATSAPP_CALL.TITLE: WhatsApp call
WHATSAPP_CALL.BODY: Lets you answer voice calls on your WhatsApp number. Meta has to have calling enabled for that number first.

TABS.TITLE: Voice settings of the inbox
TABS.BODY: Once created, the inbox gains the Voice and Calls tabs, where you fine-tune how calls behave.

FINISH.TITLE: Ready to take calls
FINISH.BODY: Place a test call to your number: you should see it arrive in the calls panel.

INBOX_SETTINGS.NAME: Inbox settings
INBOX_SETTINGS.DESCRIPTION: Walk through an inbox's tabs: settings, collaborators, business hours, CSAT and bots.

CONCEPT.TITLE: Every inbox is tuned separately
CONCEPT.BODY: Open Settings, Inboxes and pick one. Its tabs change with the channel, but the first few are the same for all of them.

GENERAL.TITLE: Settings
GENERAL.BODY: Name, avatar, auto assignment and the general behaviour of the inbox. This is the first thing to review after creating it.

COLLABORATORS.TITLE: Collaborators
COLLABORATORS.BODY: Decide which agents and teams work this inbox. Only they see its conversations and can be assigned to them.

BUSINESS_HOURS.TITLE: Business Hours
BUSINESS_HOURS.BODY: Mark the days and hours you are available, with your timezone. Outside that window you can show an away message.

CSAT.TITLE: CSAT
CSAT.BODY: Send a satisfaction survey when the conversation is resolved. The answers feed the CSAT report.

PRE_CHAT_FORM.TITLE: Pre Chat Form
PRE_CHAT_FORM.BODY: Ask for a name, email or phone before the chat starts. It gives you context and a way to reply if the visitor leaves.

CONFIGURATION.TITLE: Configuration
CONFIGURATION.BODY: The technical side of the channel: credentials, webhooks and, for email, the IMAP and SMTP servers.

BOT.TITLE: Bot Configuration
BOT.BODY: Connect a bot that answers first and hands the conversation to a person when it needs one.

FINISH.TITLE: Inbox ready
FINISH.BODY: Review these tabs whenever you create an inbox: they prevent most of the day-one surprises.

WHATSAPP_TEMPLATES.NAME: WhatsApp templates
WHATSAPP_TEMPLATES.DESCRIPTION: Review the approved templates of your WhatsApp numbers and learn when to use them.

CONCEPT.TITLE: Why templates exist
CONCEPT.BODY: WhatsApp only lets you write first with a message Meta has approved. Those templates are what this screen lists.

NAVIGATION.TITLE: Settings, Templates
NAVIGATION.BODY: Open Settings in the sidebar and go to Templates. They sync themselves from your WhatsApp inboxes.

LIST.TITLE: Your templates
LIST.BODY: Each row shows the name, language, category and body of the template, along with the inboxes where it is available.

SEARCH.TITLE: Search and filter
SEARCH.BODY: Search by content or name and filter by inbox or language when you run several numbers or several markets.

STATUS.TITLE: Status matters
STATUS.BODY: You can only send approved templates. If one shows as rejected or pending, it has to be fixed with your provider.

PREVIEW.TITLE: Preview
PREVIEW.BODY: Open a template to see it exactly as the customer will, with its buttons and its variables.

MANAGE.TITLE: Create and edit
MANAGE.BODY: This screen is read-only. To create or change a template use Manage in Meta or Manage in Twilio, depending on your provider.

USE.TITLE: Using them in a reply
USE.BODY: Inside a WhatsApp conversation the editor has a templates button: pick one, fill in its variables and send.

FINISH.TITLE: Templates mastered
FINISH.BODY: Keep the ones you use most approved and you will be able to reopen conversations outside the 24-hour window.

AGENTS.NAME: Agents
AGENTS.DESCRIPTION: Invite your team, assign roles and manage who is allowed to reply in your account.

CONCEPT.TITLE: Who answers your customers
CONCEPT.BODY: An agent is someone on your team who can read and reply to the account's messages. Before you share the workload, they need access.

WHERE.TITLE: Settings → Agents
WHERE.BODY: Adding and removing people all happens here. It is an admin-only section: agents never see it in their own sidebar.

PAGE.TITLE: The agent list
PAGE.BODY: Each row shows the name, the email, the role and whether the invitation was confirmed. The search box filters by name or email.

ADD.TITLE: Add agent
ADD.BODY: This button opens the form: agent name, agent type and email address. That is all it takes to send out the invitation.

ROLES.TITLE: Administrator or Agent
ROLES.BODY: An Administrator reaches Settings, reports and billing. An Agent only works conversations and contacts. Keep administrators few.

INVITATION.TITLE: Verification pending
INVITATION.BODY: Until the person accepts the invitation email they stay pending and cannot sign in. If it never arrives, ask them to check their spam.

MANAGE.TITLE: Edit, remove and passwords
MANAGE.BODY: From each row you can change the name, the role and the availability, reset the password, or remove the agent from the account.

FINISH.TITLE: Your team has access
FINISH.BODY: With the agents in place, the next step is organising them: create teams so conversations are routed by area.

TEAMS.NAME: Teams
TEAMS.DESCRIPTION: Group your agents by area so conversations are routed and followed without stepping on each other.

CONCEPT.TITLE: Group people by responsibility
CONCEPT.BODY: A team gathers the agents who handle the same thing: Sales, Support, Billing. One agent can belong to several teams at once.

WHERE.TITLE: Settings → Teams
WHERE.BODY: This is where you create, edit and delete teams. Only administrators can open this screen.

PAGE.TITLE: The team list
PAGE.BODY: Every team shows its name and its description. From the row you can open its settings or delete it.

CREATE.TITLE: Create a new team
CREATE.BODY: This button opens the wizard. Start with the name, such as Sales or Support, and a short description of what the team handles.

WIZARD.TITLE: Three steps and done
WIZARD.BODY: Create, Add agents and Finish. The second step is where you pick the members; you can change them later from the team settings.

AUTO_ASSIGN.TITLE: Team auto assignment
AUTO_ASSIGN.BODY: Turn auto assignment on and conversations routed to the team are shared out on their own among the available agents.

IN_SIDEBAR.TITLE: Where their work shows up
IN_SIDEBAR.BODY: Expand Conversations and you will find the Teams subgroup: every team gets its own inbox with everything assigned to it.

FINISH.TITLE: Teams are ready
FINISH.BODY: You can now assign a conversation to a whole team instead of one person. Deleting a team clears that assignment from its conversations.

CUSTOM_ROLES.NAME: Custom roles
CUSTOM_ROLES.DESCRIPTION: Build roles with the exact permissions you need when Administrator and Agent fall short.

CONCEPT.TITLE: When two roles are not enough
CONCEPT.BODY: Administrator and Agent cover the basics. A custom role opens only what you need: seeing reports, say, without touching Settings.

WHERE.TITLE: Settings → Custom roles
WHERE.BODY: This is where you define the tailored roles of your account. The feature is available on the paid plans.

PAGE.TITLE: The role list
PAGE.BODY: Each row shows the name, the description and the permissions it grants. From there you can edit or delete it.

CREATE.TITLE: Create a role
CREATE.BODY: This button opens the form: name, description and the permissions you want to tick. Name the role after the job, not the person.

PERMISSIONS.TITLE: The available permissions
PERMISSIONS.BODY: Manage all conversations, only unassigned ones or only participating ones; plus manage contacts, reports and the knowledge base.

ASSIGN.TITLE: How to assign one
ASSIGN.BODY: Go to Settings → Agents, edit the agent and pick the role under agent type. Someone on a custom role is not an administrator.

FINISH.TITLE: Permissions that fit
FINISH.BODY: Start with few roles and add permissions only when they are truly needed. Opening access is always easier than taking it back.

AGENT_BOTS.NAME: Bots
AGENT_BOTS.DESCRIPTION: Connect a webhook bot to an inbox so it handles first contact and hands off to your team.

CONCEPT.TITLE: A teammate that never sleeps
CONCEPT.BODY: A bot receives the messages of one inbox, answers the repetitive part and passes the conversation to a person when needed.

WHERE.TITLE: Settings → Bots
WHERE.BODY: This is where you register and manage the bots of the account. It is an admin-only screen.

PAGE.TITLE: The bot list
PAGE.BODY: Each row shows the bot details and its webhook URL. System bots are flagged as such and cannot be edited.

CREATE.TITLE: Add bot
CREATE.BODY: This button opens the form: avatar, bot name, description and the webhook URL we will send the events to.

WEBHOOK.TITLE: How the webhook works
WEBHOOK.BODY: Every new message is posted to your URL as an event and your service replies through the API. Keep the secret to verify each event.

CONNECT.TITLE: Connect it to an inbox
CONNECT.BODY: A bot does nothing until you assign it. Open Settings → Inboxes, pick the inbox and use its bot configuration tab.

HANDOFF.TITLE: When a human takes over
HANDOFF.BODY: The bot can close the case or leave the conversation open for an agent. Decide that boundary before it faces real customers.

FINISH.TITLE: Bot up and running
FINISH.BODY: Try it first on a low-volume inbox and review the conversations it handled before rolling it out to the rest.

LABELS.NAME: Labels
LABELS.DESCRIPTION: Create the categories you classify conversations and contacts with, and pick which reach the menu.

CONCEPT.TITLE: Your account's vocabulary
CONCEPT.BODY: Labels classify conversations and contacts: sale, complaint, shipping. The whole team shares them, so define them carefully.

WHERE.TITLE: Settings → Labels
WHERE.BODY: Every label in the account is created and edited here. Agents apply them, but only an administrator defines them.

PAGE.TITLE: The label list
PAGE.BODY: Each row shows the name, the description and the colour. The search box at the top helps once the list gets long.

CREATE.TITLE: Add label
CREATE.BODY: This button opens the form: name, description, colour and the option to show the label in the sidebar.

NAMING.TITLE: How to name them
NAMING.BODY: Only letters, numbers, hyphen and underscore are allowed, with at least two characters. Keep them few and singular: forty labels help nobody.

IN_SIDEBAR.TITLE: Labels in the menu
IN_SIDEBAR.BODY: The ones you mark for the sidebar appear under Conversations, in the Labels subgroup, as a one-click filter.

USES.TITLE: More than decoration
USES.BODY: Labels let you filter the list, measure in the Labels report and trigger automations. Without them there is no data to analyse.

FINISH.TITLE: Your taxonomy is set
FINISH.BODY: Revisit your labels every few months: merge the ones that overlap and delete the ones nobody applies.

CANNED_RESPONSES.NAME: Canned responses
CANNED_RESPONSES.DESCRIPTION: Save the messages you keep repeating and drop them into a conversation with a short shortcut.

CONCEPT.TITLE: Stop typing the same thing
CONCEPT.BODY: A canned response is a message you save once and reuse forever: the greeting, the opening hours, the status of a shipment.

WHERE.TITLE: Settings → Canned responses
WHERE.BODY: This is where you create and edit them. Unlike most Settings sections, agents can come in here and add their own.

PAGE.TITLE: The response list
PAGE.BODY: Each row shows the short code and the content of the message. They are shared: whatever you create, the whole team can use.

CREATE.TITLE: Add canned response
CREATE.BODY: This button opens a form with two fields: the short code you call it by and the message that gets inserted.

SHORT_CODE.TITLE: Pick the short code well
SHORT_CODE.BODY: Keep it short and predictable: greeting, shipping, warranty. With many of them, group by prefix: shipping-delay, shipping-swap.

USE.TITLE: Insert it by typing /
USE.BODY: In the conversation editor type / and the short code. The list appears, you pick one and the text lands ready to edit.

MANAGE.TITLE: Keep the list tidy
MANAGE.BODY: Edit or delete each response from its row. Review the wording whenever your prices, deadlines or policies change.

FINISH.TITLE: Responses ready
FINISH.BODY: Write the answer once and write it well, and the whole team answers just as well. Macros are the natural next step.

MACROS.NAME: Macros
MACROS.DESCRIPTION: Chain several actions (reply, label, assign, resolve) and run them all with a single click.

CONCEPT.TITLE: Several actions, one click
CONCEPT.BODY: A macro is a saved sequence of actions on a conversation. Where you used to do five things in a row, now you do one.

WHERE.TITLE: Settings → Macros
WHERE.BODY: Every macro in the account lives here. Agents come in too: they can create their own private ones.

PAGE.TITLE: The macro list
PAGE.BODY: Each row shows the name, who created it, the last update and its visibility. From there you can view, edit or delete it.

EDITOR.TITLE: The macro editor
EDITOR.BODY: This is a brand-new macro: give it a name and add actions between the start and the end of the flow.

ACTIONS.TITLE: What a macro can do
ACTIONS.BODY: Send a message, add or remove labels, assign an agent or team, change priority, snooze, resolve, or email the transcript.

ORDER.TITLE: Order matters
ORDER.BODY: Actions run in the order you add them. Drag them by the handle to rearrange: reply first, resolve last.

VISIBILITY.TITLE: Public or private
VISIBILITY.BODY: A public macro is available to every agent and only administrators can create one. A private macro is yours alone.

RUN.TITLE: How to run it
RUN.BODY: Open a conversation and look for Macros in the right panel. Preview it first if you want to see exactly what will happen.

FINISH.TITLE: Turn routine into one click
FINISH.BODY: If you repeat the same sequence three times a day, make it a macro. We are back on the list so you can build your first one.

AUTOMATION_RULES.NAME: Automation rules
AUTOMATION_RULES.DESCRIPTION: Rules that run on their own: when something happens and your conditions match, the system acts.

CONCEPT.TITLE: If this happens, do that
CONCEPT.BODY: A rule watches what happens in your conversations and acts on its own. Nobody has to remember to label, assign or notify.

WHERE.TITLE: Settings → Automation
WHERE.BODY: Every rule in the account is created and managed here. It is an admin-only section.

PAGE.TITLE: The rule list
PAGE.BODY: Each row shows the name, whether it is active and when it was created. A disabled rule is kept but never runs.

CREATE.TITLE: Create a rule
CREATE.BODY: This button opens the form. You need four things: a name, a description, the event that fires it and the actions to run.

EVENT.TITLE: The event that fires it
EVENT.BODY: Conversation created, updated, opened or resolved, and message created. Changing the event resets the conditions you already wrote.

CONDITIONS.TITLE: The conditions
CONDITIONS.BODY: They narrow down when it applies: the inbox, the sender, the message content, labels or your custom attributes. At least one is required.

ACTIONS.TITLE: The actions
ACTIONS.BODY: Assign an agent or team, add labels, change the priority, send a message or a note, email someone, or call a webhook.

DELAYED.TITLE: Run after a wait
DELAYED.BODY: A rule can wait and run only if nothing changed: warn you, for instance, when a customer has gone two hours without a reply.

MANAGE.TITLE: Enable, clone and delete
MANAGE.BODY: From the list you enable or disable each rule, clone it to build a variant, or delete it. Cloning beats starting from scratch.

FINISH.TITLE: Let the system work for you
FINISH.BODY: Start with one simple rule and check it against real conversations before adding more. A badly written rule shows up fast.

SLA.NAME: Service level agreements
SLA.DESCRIPTION: Set how fast you promise to reply and resolve, and catch what is slipping while there is still time.

CONCEPT.TITLE: A promise you can measure
CONCEPT.BODY: An SLA sets the times you promise your customers. The system watches them and flags the conversation as the deadline nears or passes.

WHERE.TITLE: Settings → SLA
WHERE.BODY: This is where you create and manage SLA policies. The feature is available on the paid plans.

PAGE.TITLE: The policy list
PAGE.BODY: Each row shows the policy name, its thresholds and whether it follows business hours. You can keep several for different customers.

CREATE.TITLE: Add SLA
CREATE.BODY: This button opens the form: name, description and the three time thresholds. Start with one general policy for everyone.

THRESHOLDS.TITLE: The three thresholds
THRESHOLDS.BODY: First response time, next response time and resolution time. Set only the ones you are genuinely going to honour.

BUSINESS_HOURS.TITLE: Business hours only
BUSINESS_HOURS.BODY: Switch it on and the clock stops outside your working hours. Without it, a Saturday message burns the deadline while nobody works.

APPLY.TITLE: How it reaches a case
APPLY.BODY: The policy is attached to the conversation from the right panel or by an automation, based on the inbox or the customer's label.

TRACK.TITLE: Knowing whether you comply
TRACK.BODY: The conversation header shows the time left, and the SLA report gathers every miss so you can review them with the team.

FINISH.TITLE: Deadlines under control
FINISH.BODY: Start with times you already meet today and tune them with the report. An impossible SLA only creates alarms nobody looks at.

CONVERSATION_WORKFLOW.NAME: Conversation workflow
CONVERSATION_WORKFLOW.DESCRIPTION: Tune how conversations close: automatic resolution and data that is mandatory before resolving.

CONCEPT.TITLE: How a conversation closes
CONCEPT.BODY: This section covers two things: when forgotten conversations resolve on their own, and what data you require before a case is closed.

WHERE.TITLE: Settings → Conversation Workflow
WHERE.BODY: The menu lists it as Conversation Workflow. This is an admin screen and whatever you set here affects the whole account.

PAGE.TITLE: Two blocks of settings
PAGE.BODY: The page holds automatic resolution and required attributes. Each block only appears if your plan includes it.

AUTO_RESOLVE.TITLE: Automatic resolution
AUTO_RESOLVE.BODY: It resolves any conversation that has gone too long without activity, so your inbox stops filling up with dead cases.

AUTO_RESOLVE_OPTIONS.TITLE: Tune it before turning it on
AUTO_RESOLVE_OPTIONS.BODY: Pick the inactivity time, a closing message for the customer, a label to tag it, and whether to skip those awaiting a reply.

REQUIRED_ATTRIBUTES.TITLE: Data required on resolution
REQUIRED_ATTRIBUTES.BODY: Choose which custom attributes cannot be left empty. It keeps the contact reason and the order number from getting lost.

REQUIRED_FLOW.TITLE: What the agent sees
REQUIRED_FLOW.BODY: On resolve, if any of those fields is missing a short form asks for them. The conversation stays open until it is filled in.

FINISH.TITLE: Consistent closures
FINISH.BODY: With these two settings your conversations close on time and with complete information. Your reports will thank you.

LUXOIA_OVERVIEW.NAME: Get started with LuxoIA
LUXOIA_OVERVIEW.DESCRIPTION: What LuxoIA is, where it lives in the menu, and how to read your assistant's overview.

SIDEBAR.TITLE: LuxoIA in the sidebar
SIDEBAR.BODY: LuxoIA is the AI assistant that answers customers on its own. Open this group in the sidebar to reach every one of its sections.

SECTIONS.TITLE: The LuxoIA sections
SECTIONS.BODY: Overview, FAQs, Documents, Scenarios, Playground, Inboxes, Tools and Settings. Each one has its own tutorial in this library.

PAGE.TITLE: The assistant overview
PAGE.BODY: This screen sums up how your assistant worked. Pick the period from the selector at the top right: last 7 days, last 30 days or this month.

METRICS.TITLE: The metrics that matter
METRICS.BODY: Conversations handled, auto-resolution rate, handoff rate, reopens and hours saved. Administrators can click a card to see the conversations behind it.

KNOWLEDGE.TITLE: Knowledge coverage
KNOWLEDGE.BODY: Shows how much your assistant knows: approved FAQs, pending suggestions and documents. The higher the coverage, the fewer questions reach an agent.

SWITCHER.TITLE: Switch assistants
SWITCHER.BODY: Next to the page title you'll see the active assistant's name with a chevron. Use it to move between assistants when you have more than one.

CREATE.TITLE: Create a new assistant
CREATE.BODY: That same switcher offers Create Assistant. You only need a name, a description and the product it answers about; everything else is tuned later.

FINISH.TITLE: You know your way around
FINISH.BODY: The next step is giving it knowledge: start with the FAQs tutorial, then the Documents one.

LUXOIA_FAQS.NAME: LuxoIA FAQs
LUXOIA_FAQS.DESCRIPTION: How to write the answers your assistant uses and approve the suggestions it proposes.

NAV.TITLE: The FAQs section
NAV.BODY: This is where your assistant's knowledge lives: question-and-answer pairs it uses to reply. It is the section you will visit most.

PAGE.TITLE: The FAQ list
PAGE.BODY: Each card shows the question, the answer and how many conversations used it. That counter tells you which ones are worth improving.

CREATE.TITLE: Create an FAQ
CREATE.BODY: The plus button at the top right adds a question and its answer. Write the question the way a customer would ask it, not the way you would.

SEARCH.TITLE: Search and prune
SEARCH.BODY: The search box filters by text. Hover a card to select it, then bulk-delete the answers that went stale.

SUGGESTIONS.TITLE: FAQ suggestions
SUGGESTIONS.BODY: LuxoIA groups your customers' repeated questions and proposes new FAQs. When there are some, a blue banner offers Review suggestions.

APPROVE.TITLE: Approve or dismiss
APPROVE.BODY: In the review queue you can open the source conversations, fix the wording and approve. Approved items move straight into the FAQ list.

QUALITY.TITLE: One answer, one idea
QUALITY.BODY: Short, concrete answers work better than long text. If a question covers two topics, split it into two FAQs.

FINISH.TITLE: Knowledge is in place
FINISH.BODY: Try what you just loaded in the Playground and, if something is missing, add it as a document.

LUXOIA_DOCUMENTS.NAME: LuxoIA documents
LUXOIA_DOCUMENTS.DESCRIPTION: How to feed the assistant with web pages and PDFs, and keep that content up to date.

NAV.TITLE: The Documents section
NAV.BODY: Instead of writing every FAQ by hand, you give LuxoIA a whole source: a web page or a PDF. It extracts the questions and answers for you.

PAGE.TITLE: Your knowledge sources
PAGE.BODY: Each card is one document with its origin, its status and how many FAQs it produced. The filters above split web pages from PDFs.

ADD.TITLE: Add a document
ADD.BODY: The plus button takes a page URL or a PDF upload. Pick pages with stable information: pricing, shipping policies, support questions.

STATUS.TITLE: Status and generated FAQs
STATUS.BODY: After the upload the document is processed and you see how many FAQs came out of it. That number tells you whether the source was useful.

SYNC.TITLE: Keep it up to date
SYNC.BODY: When the page changes, the document is flagged as Needs update. Select it and use Refresh so LuxoIA reads the source again.

REVIEW.TITLE: Review what it learned
