REVIEW.BODY: Generated answers land in the FAQs section. Open it and fix anything wrong before a customer reads it.

FINISH.TITLE: Sources under control
FINISH.BODY: With documents and FAQs current, your assistant answers with real information. Set when and to whom it replies in Settings.

LUXOIA_SCENARIOS.NAME: LuxoIA scenarios
LUXOIA_SCENARIOS.DESCRIPTION: How to instruct your assistant for concrete situations, like a refund or a complaint.

NAV.TITLE: The Scenarios section
NAV.BODY: An FAQ answers a question. A scenario tells the assistant how to act in a situation: what to ask, what to check and when to hand off.

PAGE.TITLE: Your scenarios
PAGE.BODY: Each card is one situation with its instruction. The search box helps as the list grows, and you can select several and delete them together.

EXAMPLES.TITLE: Start from the examples
EXAMPLES.BODY: The first time you'll see a list of example scenarios. Add one with a click and edit it: faster than starting from a blank page.

CREATE.TITLE: Create a scenario
CREATE.BODY: It needs a title, a description of when it applies and the step-by-step instruction. Write it as you would brief a new agent.

TOOLS.TITLE: Scenarios with tools
TOOLS.BODY: A scenario can call the tools from the Tools section to query your own system, for example to look up an order's status.

FINISH.TITLE: Situations covered
FINISH.BODY: Test every scenario in the Playground with the message a real customer would send before leaving it live.

LUXOIA_PLAYGROUND.NAME: LuxoIA playground
LUXOIA_PLAYGROUND.DESCRIPTION: How to test your assistant's answers before it talks to a real customer.

NAV.TITLE: The playground
NAV.BODY: The playground is a private chat with your assistant. Nothing you type here reaches a customer or creates a conversation.

PAGE.TITLE: Talk to your assistant
PAGE.BODY: Type below and send. It answers with the same knowledge and the same rules it will use in production.

WHAT_TO_ASK.TITLE: What to ask it
WHAT_TO_ASK.BODY: Use real customer questions, typos included. Also try the things it should refuse to answer, so you can see where its limits are.

FIX.TITLE: When an answer is wrong
FIX.BODY: If it replies badly, fix the FAQ it used, add a document with the missing data, or write a scenario for that situation.

CREDITS.TITLE: It uses credits
CREDITS.BODY: Messages you send here count toward your LuxoIA credits, just like a real conversation. Test what you need, not more.

FINISH.TITLE: Ready for production
FINISH.BODY: Once the answers convince you, connect the assistant to an inbox from the Inboxes section.

LUXOIA_INBOXES.NAME: LuxoIA inboxes
LUXOIA_INBOXES.DESCRIPTION: How to connect your assistant to an inbox so it starts answering customers.

NAV.TITLE: The Inboxes section
NAV.BODY: An assistant with no inbox connected answers nobody. Here you choose the channels it works on: website, WhatsApp, email or any other.

PAGE.TITLE: Connected inboxes
PAGE.BODY: Each card is an inbox where the assistant already replies. An empty list means your assistant is trained but switched off.

CONNECT.TITLE: Connect an inbox
CONNECT.BODY: The plus button lets you pick the inbox. Start with a single low-volume one and watch how it answers for a few days.

HANDOFF.TITLE: When your team steps in
HANDOFF.BODY: If the customer asks for a person or the assistant does not know, it hands the conversation over and your team sees it like any other.

DISCONNECT.TITLE: Disconnect
DISCONNECT.BODY: Each card's menu has Disconnect. The assistant stops replying on that channel instantly, without losing any of its knowledge.

FINISH.TITLE: Your assistant is live
FINISH.BODY: Come back to the Overview in a few days to see how many conversations it resolved on its own and where it still needs help.

LUXOIA_SETTINGS.NAME: LuxoIA settings
LUXOIA_SETTINGS.DESCRIPTION: Name, messages, who it answers, on what schedule and which topics it may cover.

NAV.TITLE: The Settings section
NAV.BODY: Everything that defines your assistant's character lives here, organised in the tab rail on the left of the screen.

PAGE.TITLE: Basic settings
PAGE.BODY: The first tab holds the name, the description, the product it talks about, and the welcome, handoff and closing messages.

SYSTEM.TITLE: When the customer goes quiet
SYSTEM.BODY: System settings decides what happens when a conversation goes silent: wait for the customer, always resolve, or let LuxoIA review it first.

AUDIENCE.TITLE: Who it answers
AUDIENCE.BODY: Audience lets you choose between everyone and only the customers matching conditions, such as a language or a contact attribute.

SCHEDULE.TITLE: When it answers
SCHEDULE.BODY: Schedule sets whether it works anytime, only during business hours or only outside them. Inboxes with no business hours stay always covered.

GUARDRAILS.TITLE: Limits on what it answers
GUARDRAILS.BODY: Guardrails marks the topics the assistant must stay away from: legal advice, discount promises or anything sensitive.

GUIDELINES.TITLE: The tone of its replies
GUIDELINES.BODY: Response guidelines define how it writes: formal or friendly, brief or detailed. Both lists ship with examples you can add in one click.

DELETE.TITLE: Delete the assistant
DELETE.BODY: The red delete button sits at the bottom of the first tab. It removes its FAQs and documents too, so use it carefully.

FINISH.TITLE: Assistant tuned
FINISH.BODY: Every change shows up in the next conversation. Test in the Playground after touching the tone or the limits.

LUXOIA_TOOLS.NAME: LuxoIA tools
LUXOIA_TOOLS.DESCRIPTION: How to connect your assistant to your own APIs so it can fetch data and take actions.

NAV.TITLE: The Tools section
NAV.BODY: A tool gives the assistant access to your system: look up an order, check a payment or open a ticket without leaving the chat.

PAGE.TITLE: Your tools
PAGE.BODY: Each card shows the endpoint, the HTTP method and the authentication type. You can switch a tool off without deleting it.

CREATE.TITLE: Create a tool
CREATE.BODY: You need a title, a description, the endpoint URL, the method and the parameters. The description matters most: it decides when the tool is used.

AUTH.TITLE: Authentication
AUTH.BODY: Set how the call to your API authenticates. Use a read-only credential scoped to what the assistant actually needs.

SCENARIOS.TITLE: Use them in a scenario
SCENARIOS.BODY: Tools are triggered from scenarios: there you describe when the assistant should call them and what to do with the answer.

LIMIT.TITLE: Few and well described
LIMIT.BODY: Past ten tools the assistant starts picking the wrong one. Delete what you no longer use before adding another.

FINISH.TITLE: Assistant connected
FINISH.BODY: Test each tool in the Playground with a real case and check that it returns exactly the data you expected.

CALLS.NAME: Calls
CALLS.DESCRIPTION: How to call from a conversation and review your team's call history.

CALL_BUTTON.TITLE: Call from the conversation
CALL_BUTTON.BODY: When the inbox has a voice channel, this button dials the contact without leaving the chat. The call stays linked to this conversation.

WIDGET.TITLE: The call panel
WIDGET.BODY: While the call runs, a floating panel shows the timer, the mute control and the hang-up button. You can keep typing as you talk.

DASHBOARD.TITLE: The call history
DASHBOARD.BODY: Calls in the sidebar gathers everything that came in and went out through your voice channels, whoever answered it.

PAGE.TITLE: The call list
PAGE.BODY: Each row shows who called, who answered, how long it lasted and how it ended. Open one to reach the conversation behind it.

FILTERS.TITLE: Filter what matters
FILTERS.BODY: Missed and No reply are the two filters you will use most. More filters narrows the list down by inbox.

ASSIGNEE.TITLE: Who answered
ASSIGNEE.BODY: Administrators can filter by assignee and review each agent's load. Agents only ever see their own calls.

SETUP.TITLE: If you see no calls
SETUP.BODY: The history needs at least one inbox with a voice channel configured. Ask an administrator for it if the screen stays empty.

FINISH.TITLE: Calls under control
FINISH.BODY: Check the missed ones at the start of the day: those are customers who tried to reach you and are still waiting.

CAMPAIGN_LIVE_CHAT.NAME: Live chat campaigns
CAMPAIGN_LIVE_CHAT.DESCRIPTION: Create messages that appear on their own in your website chat when someone visits a page.

CONCEPT.TITLE: Speaking first on your site
CONCEPT.BODY: A live chat campaign fires a message in your website chat when a visitor meets a condition. It picks up interest without waiting for them to write first.

WHERE.TITLE: Where these campaigns live
WHERE.BODY: In the menu, Campaigns → Live Chat. Each campaign type has its own screen and its own rules, so start from the one you actually need.

PAGE.TITLE: The live chat screen
PAGE.BODY: This lists the campaigns you already created and whether each one is enabled or disabled. Edit or delete them at any time without touching the conversations they started.

CREATE.TITLE: The Create campaign button
CREATE.BODY: Top right, Create campaign opens the form. Start with a single well-aimed campaign before filling your site with pop-up messages.

FORM.TITLE: The campaign form
FORM.BODY: Here you set the Title, which stays internal, the Message the visitor reads, and the website inbox it is sent from. No inbox, no campaign.

TRIGGER.TITLE: When it fires
TRIGGER.BODY: URL is the page address it watches, and Time on page is how many seconds it waits before showing up. Ten seconds is usually enough.

SENDER.TITLE: Who sends it, and when
SENDER.BODY: Sent by picks a bot or an agent: that is the name the customer sees. Other preferences let you enable the campaign and limit it to business hours.

LIST.TITLE: Check what is already live
LIST.BODY: Each card shows the message, the inbox, the sender and the URL that triggers it. If a campaign is not working, turn it off before adding another.

FINISH.TITLE: Your live chat campaign is set
FINISH.BODY: You can create, trigger and review. Replies land as ordinary conversations, so tell your team before you switch a campaign on.

CAMPAIGN_SMS.NAME: SMS campaigns
CAMPAIGN_SMS.DESCRIPTION: Send a text message to a group of contacts at the date and time you choose.

CONCEPT.TITLE: One message, one list, one date
CONCEPT.BODY: An SMS campaign is a single send to a group of contacts. It does not repeat: you schedule it, it goes out, it stays on record. You need a connected SMS inbox.

WHERE.TITLE: Where SMS campaigns live
WHERE.BODY: In the menu, Campaigns → SMS. Only text sends show up here; live chat and WhatsApp have screens of their own.

PAGE.TITLE: The SMS screen
PAGE.BODY: It lists your sends with their status: scheduled while they wait for the hour, completed once they went out. A completed send cannot be undone.

CREATE.TITLE: The Create campaign button
CREATE.BODY: Top right, Create campaign opens the form. Have the copy and the contact list ready: confirming the form schedules the send.

FORM.TITLE: The send form
FORM.BODY: You set a Title to recognise it internally, the Message the customer receives, and the SMS inbox it goes out from. Keep it short: it is a text message.

AUDIENCE.TITLE: Who receives it
AUDIENCE.BODY: Audience is built from contact labels, not from individual people. Label your contacts first: sending to everyone annoys people and costs you subscribers.

SCHEDULE.TITLE: When it goes out
SCHEDULE.BODY: Scheduled time sets the date and hour of the send. Pick a sensible slot for your audience: a text at midnight reads as spam.

STATUS.TITLE: Following the send
STATUS.BODY: Each card shows the inbox it left from and the date. Customer replies arrive as new conversations in that same inbox.

FINISH.TITLE: Your SMS send is ready
FINISH.BODY: You can write, segment and schedule. Start with a small group, measure the replies, and only then widen the audience.

CAMPAIGN_WHATSAPP.NAME: WhatsApp campaigns
CAMPAIGN_WHATSAPP.DESCRIPTION: Send WhatsApp-approved templates to a group of contacts and measure delivery.

CONCEPT.TITLE: WhatsApp requires a template
CONCEPT.BODY: To message first on WhatsApp you cannot use free text: you have to send a template approved by Meta. These are the most-read messages you have, so use them carefully.

WHERE.TITLE: Where these campaigns live
WHERE.BODY: In the menu, Campaigns → WhatsApp. You need a connected WhatsApp inbox; if you do not have one, create it first under Settings → Inboxes.

PAGE.TITLE: The WhatsApp screen
PAGE.BODY: It lists your sends with their status: scheduled while they wait for the hour, completed once they went out. From a sent campaign you can open its analytics.

TEMPLATES.TITLE: Get the template ready first
TEMPLATES.BODY: Templates are managed under Settings → Templates and approved by Meta, not by LuxoInbox. Without an approved template you cannot create the campaign.

CREATE.TITLE: The Create campaign button
CREATE.BODY: Top right, Create campaign opens the form. Keep the approved template and the audience labels you want to reach at hand.

FORM.TITLE: The send form
FORM.BODY: You set the internal Title, pick the WhatsApp inbox and choose the template to send. The preview shows exactly how the message will arrive.

VARIABLES.TITLE: Fill in the variables
VARIABLES.BODY: If the template has placeholders, the form asks for a value for each one. Check them: a badly filled placeholder reaches the customer as it is.

AUDIENCE.TITLE: Who receives it
AUDIENCE.BODY: Audience is built from contact labels, and Scheduled time sets the date of the send. Segment properly: WhatsApp penalises blind mass sends.

ANALYTICS.TITLE: Measure delivery
ANALYTICS.BODY: On a processed campaign, the analytics option opens the breakdown of delivered, read and failed messages. That detail tells you whether the list or the copy failed.

FINISH.TITLE: Your WhatsApp campaign is set
FINISH.BODY: You can prepare the template, segment, schedule and measure. Every reply lands as a conversation in the WhatsApp inbox you picked.

PORTAL_SETUP.NAME: Set up your portal
PORTAL_SETUP.DESCRIPTION: Build the public help center portal: name, domain, appearance and languages.

CONCEPT.TITLE: A site that answers for you
CONCEPT.BODY: The help center is a public site holding your articles. Every question answered there is a conversation your team never has to handle.

WHERE.TITLE: Where it is managed
WHERE.BODY: The whole help center hangs off this menu group: articles, categories, locales and settings. Content always belongs to a portal.

CREATE.TITLE: Create your first portal
CREATE.BODY: A portal is a complete site. Create Portal starts the wizard: basic information first, then customisation, and you are done.

BASICS.TITLE: Name, slug and domain
BASICS.BODY: The Name is internal, the Slug builds the public address, and a Custom domain is only needed if you want to serve the portal from your own site.

CUSTOMIZATION.TITLE: How the portal looks
CUSTOMIZATION.BODY: Customisation is where you upload the Logo, pick the Theme color and write the portal Title and sub text. It is the first thing a visitor sees.

SWITCHER.TITLE: More than one portal
SWITCHER.BODY: You can run one portal per product or per brand. The portal name sits at the top left, and the arrow beside it switches between them.

SETTINGS.TITLE: Portal settings
SETTINGS.BODY: This is where you edit everything you set at creation, manage the available locales and decide which one is the default.

PUBLISH.TITLE: Publish and visit
PUBLISH.BODY: From settings you can open the live portal with Visit site. Look at it the way a customer would before you share the link.

FINISH.TITLE: Your portal is standing
FINISH.BODY: You now have somewhere to publish. Next comes filling it: the Articles walkthrough shows you how to write and publish the first one.

ARTICLES.NAME: Articles
ARTICLES.DESCRIPTION: Write, organise, publish and translate the articles in your help center.

CONCEPT.TITLE: The help center content
CONCEPT.BODY: An article answers one specific question. Write one for each real customer question, not a giant manual nobody finishes reading.

WHERE.TITLE: Where the articles are
WHERE.BODY: In the menu, Help Center → Articles. You are always looking at the articles of one portal in one language.

PAGE.TITLE: The article list
PAGE.BODY: Search and the category and locale filters sit at the top. Below them, the list with each article's status and view count.

TABS.TITLE: Filter by status
TABS.BODY: The tabs split All articles, Mine, Draft, Published and Archived. Start with Draft: that is where the half-finished work sits.

CARD.TITLE: One article's row
CARD.BODY: Each row shows title, category, status and how many times it was read. The menu on the right lets you publish, move to draft, archive, translate or delete.

NEW.TITLE: Write a new one
NEW.BODY: The New article button, top right, opens an empty editor inside the portal and the language you currently have selected.

EDITOR.TITLE: The editor
EDITOR.BODY: You write the title and the body with formatting, images and links. It saves on its own: you will see Saving and then Saved at the top.

PUBLISH.TITLE: Draft, published, archived
PUBLISH.BODY: An article starts as a draft and stays private until you hit Publish. Move to archived takes it off the portal without deleting it, which suits outdated content.

TRANSLATE.TITLE: Translate to another language
TRANSLATE.BODY: Tick one or more articles and use Translate to create the version in another language. They arrive as drafts, so review them before publishing.

FINISH.TITLE: You can publish now
FINISH.BODY: Write few articles and good ones, check every quarter which are actually read, and archive whatever no longer applies. A stale help center hurts.

CATEGORIES_AND_LOCALES.NAME: Categories and locales
CATEGORIES_AND_LOCALES.DESCRIPTION: Organise articles into categories and publish your portal in several languages.

CONCEPT.TITLE: Order and translation
CONCEPT.BODY: Categories group articles so customers can find them; locales serve the same portal to different audiences. They are set up separately.

CATEGORIES.TITLE: Where the categories are
CATEGORIES.BODY: In the menu, Help Center → Categories. Categories belong to one portal and one locale: each locale has its own set.

CATEGORY_PAGE.TITLE: The category list
CATEGORY_PAGE.BODY: Each card shows the name, the description and how many articles it holds. Click one to see and reorder its articles.

NEW_CATEGORY.TITLE: Create a category
NEW_CATEGORY.BODY: New category asks for a Name, a Slug and a Description. The name and description appear on the public portal, so write them for the customer.

ORDER.TITLE: Order matters
ORDER.BODY: Inside a category you can drag articles to decide which comes first. Put the ones that answer the most common questions at the top.

LOCALES.TITLE: Where the locales are
LOCALES.BODY: In the menu, Help Center → Locales. Each locale is a full version of the portal, with its own categories and articles.

NEW_LOCALE.TITLE: Add a locale
NEW_LOCALE.BODY: New locale lets you pick the language and whether it goes in published or as a draft. One of them is the default: the one shown when no translation exists.

CONTENT.TITLE: Tune each locale
CONTENT.BODY: Each locale menu offers Localize content, to translate the portal name and texts, and Select recommended content, for what its home page highlights.

FINISH.TITLE: A tidy portal
FINISH.BODY: A handful of clear categories and one well-kept locale is enough. Add a second locale only once the first one is complete.

REPORTS_FILTERS.NAME: Report filters
REPORTS_FILTERS.DESCRIPTION: The controls every report shares: dates, grouping, business hours and download.

CONCEPT.TITLE: One shared control panel
CONCEPT.BODY: Every report reads the same way: pick a period, decide how to group, compare. Learning these controls once covers all nine screens.

WHERE.TITLE: Where to try them
WHERE.BODY: The Conversations report shows every control at once, so we use it as the example. The same filters appear on the other reports.

HEADER.TITLE: The report header
HEADER.BODY: It tells you what you are looking at and keeps the screen's actions, such as download, on the right. Read it before drawing conclusions from a number.

DATE_RANGE.TITLE: The date range
DATE_RANGE.BODY: Choose the last 7, 14 or 30 days, a recent month, or a custom date range. Everything you see below belongs to that period only.

GROUP_BY.TITLE: Group by
GROUP_BY.BODY: Group by sets how wide each bar is: day, week, month or year. Day exposes spikes; week or month shows the real trend.

BUSINESS_HOURS.TITLE: Count only your hours
BUSINESS_HOURS.BODY: The business hours switch takes nights and weekends out of the response times. Turn it on if you do not staff around the clock: the numbers get fairer.

DOWNLOAD.TITLE: Download the report
DOWNLOAD.BODY: The download button hands you the same period as a CSV file, ready for a spreadsheet or to share outside LuxoInbox.

DRILLDOWN.TITLE: From the number to the case
DRILLDOWN.BODY: Clicking a bar in a chart opens a panel with the conversations behind it. That is how you go from an average to a concrete case.

FINISH.TITLE: You can filter now
FINISH.BODY: Set a period, group by week, and compare against the previous one. On its own, a single number tells you nothing.

REPORTS_CONVERSATIONS_AGENTS.NAME: Conversations and agents
REPORTS_CONVERSATIONS_AGENTS.DESCRIPTION: How much work arrives, how fast it is handled and how each agent is doing.

CONCEPT.TITLE: Volume and performance
CONCEPT.BODY: Two questions in a row: how much work arrives, and who is getting it done. The first is answered in Conversations, the second in Agents.

CONVERSATIONS.TITLE: The Conversations report
CONVERSATIONS.BODY: In the menu, Reports → Conversations. It is the snapshot of volume and response times over the period you choose.

CHARTS.TITLE: The charts
CHARTS.BODY: Each chart is one metric over time. Read them together: high volume with steady times means spare capacity, low volume with high times means a bottleneck.

METRICS.TITLE: What each number measures
METRICS.BODY: Conversations and messages are totals. First response time, resolution time and customer waiting time are averages: one extreme case drags them.

AGENTS.TITLE: The agent summary
AGENTS.BODY: In the menu, Reports → Agents. One row per person, with the same metrics as the previous report applied to their own work.

TABLE.TITLE: Reading the table
TABLE.BODY: Compare the conversations column with the time columns. An agent with many cases and high times is not underperforming: they are overloaded.

DETAIL.TITLE: Looking at one person
DETAIL.BODY: Clicking an agent's name opens their detail, with their own charts and date range. Use it to talk with the person, not to build rankings.

DOWNLOAD.TITLE: Download the summary
DOWNLOAD.BODY: The download button exports the whole table as CSV for the period you selected. It replaces screenshots in your monthly reviews.

FINISH.TITLE: You can measure the work
FINISH.BODY: Check volume and times once a week and share the load using data. One day's spike is noise; the trend is the signal.

REPORTS_LABELS_INBOXES_TEAMS.NAME: Labels, inboxes and teams
REPORTS_LABELS_INBOXES_TEAMS.DESCRIPTION: The same metrics sliced by label, by inbox and by team.

CONCEPT.TITLE: Three ways to slice the same data
CONCEPT.BODY: These three reports share their metrics with the agent report and only change what they group by. Pick the slice that matches the question you brought.

LABELS.TITLE: Label summary
LABELS.BODY: In the menu, Reports → Labels. It answers what your customers talk about: returns, shipping, pricing, depending on how you label conversations.

LABELS_USE.TITLE: What it is for
LABELS_USE.BODY: If a label grows month after month, you are looking at a product problem or a help center article that still needs writing.

INBOXES.TITLE: Inbox summary
INBOXES.BODY: In the menu, Reports → Inbox. It compares how each connected channel performs: website, WhatsApp, email or social.

INBOXES_USE.TITLE: What it is for
INBOXES_USE.BODY: Times usually vary a lot between channels. If one falls behind, check who staffs it and what assignment rules it has.

TEAMS.TITLE: Team overview
TEAMS.BODY: In the menu, Reports → Team. It groups the work by the teams you created rather than by person: the view for talking to their leads.

TEAMS_USE.TITLE: What it is for
TEAMS_USE.BODY: Use it to move people between teams and to spot a team carrying more than it can sustain.

DETAIL.TITLE: Opening the detail
DETAIL.BODY: In all three reports, clicking a name opens its own screen with charts over time. That is where you see whether today's number is normal or exceptional.

FINISH.TITLE: You can compare now
FINISH.BODY: Always start from the question and pick the slice afterwards. Opening all three reports without a question only costs you time.

REPORTS_CSAT_SLA_BOT.NAME: Satisfaction, SLA and bot
REPORTS_CSAT_SLA_BOT.DESCRIPTION: The quality reports: what customers think, whether you hit deadlines, what the bot solves.

CONCEPT.TITLE: Measuring quality, not volume
CONCEPT.BODY: These three reports do not count work: they tell you whether you did it well. Customer satisfaction, deadline compliance and what the bot really contributes.

CSAT.TITLE: Satisfaction surveys
CSAT.BODY: In the menu, Reports → CSAT. It collects the answers to the survey that is sent when a conversation is closed.

CSAT_METRICS.TITLE: The three key numbers
CSAT_METRICS.BODY: Total responses says how many people answered, satisfaction score what share was positive, and response rate whether the survey is reaching anyone.

CSAT_TABLE.TITLE: Read the comments
CSAT_TABLE.BODY: The table lists every response with contact, agent and rating, and you can filter by agent, inbox, team or rating. The written comments beat the average.

SLA.TITLE: SLA compliance
SLA.BODY: In the menu, Reports → SLA. It shows which conversations met the deadlines you promised and which ones missed them.

SLA_METRICS.TITLE: Hits and misses
SLA_METRICS.BODY: Hit rate is the share you met and number of misses the breaches in the period. Always open the misses: each one has a reason of its own.

BOT.TITLE: Bot reports
BOT.BODY: In the menu, Reports → Bot. It measures what the bot does before a conversation ever reaches a person.

BOT_METRICS.TITLE: Helping or getting in the way?
BOT_METRICS.BODY: Look at how many conversations it handled, how many it closed and the handoff rate. If it hands off almost everything, its answers need work.

FINISH.TITLE: You can measure quality
FINISH.BODY: A fast team with unhappy customers is not working. Cross these three reports with the volume ones before you change anything.

ACCOUNT_SETTINGS.NAME: Account settings
ACCOUNT_SETTINGS.DESCRIPTION: Set the name, the language and the basic details the whole account runs on.

CONCEPT.TITLE: Your account's identity
CONCEPT.BODY: This is where what defines the whole account lives: what it is called and which language it works in. Worth getting right first.

WHERE.TITLE: Settings → Account Settings
WHERE.BODY: Open Settings in the sidebar and go to Account settings. Only administrators can see this section.

PAGE.TITLE: General settings
PAGE.BODY: The page has one block of general details and, below it, technical information about the account. Everything saves with a single button.

NAME.TITLE: Account name
NAME.BODY: This is the name you see in the account switcher and the one that shows up in several notifications. Use your real company name.

LOCALE.TITLE: Site language
LOCALE.BODY: It sets the default dashboard language for the whole account. Each person can still change their own in Profile settings.

SAVE.TITLE: Save your changes
SAVE.BODY: Nothing is applied until you press Update settings at the end of the form. A green notice confirms it went through.

ACCOUNT_ID.TITLE: Account ID
ACCOUNT_ID.BODY: Further down you will find the Account ID. You need it when you connect the API or when support asks you to identify your account.

FINISH.TITLE: Your account is set up
FINISH.BODY: With the name and language sorted, the next step is connecting external tools from Integrations.

INTEGRATIONS.NAME: Integrations
INTEGRATIONS.DESCRIPTION: Connect LuxoInbox to other tools and push real-time events with webhooks.

CONCEPT.TITLE: Connecting your other tools
CONCEPT.BODY: An integration lets LuxoInbox read from or write to another system: your CRM, your store, your task tracker or your internal chat.

WHERE.TITLE: Settings → Integrations
WHERE.BODY: Open Settings and go to Integrations. It is an administrator-only section because it connects data from the whole account.

CATALOG.TITLE: The app catalog
CATALOG.BODY: Each card is an available app. The search box at the top filters by name once the list gets long.

CONFIGURE.TITLE: Enabled or Disabled
CONFIGURE.BODY: The label on each card tells you whether it is already connected. Press Configure to connect it, review its details or disconnect it.

WEBHOOKS.TITLE: Webhooks: live events
WEBHOOKS.BODY: A webhook notifies your system every time something happens here. Press Add new webhook and give it the URL that should receive the call.

WEBHOOK_EVENTS.TITLE: Choose which events to send
WEBHOOK_EVENTS.BODY: In the form you tick the events: conversation created, message created, contact updated and several more. Only send the ones you use.

DASHBOARD_APPS.TITLE: Dashboard Apps
DASHBOARD_APPS.BODY: A dashboard app embeds your own web page inside the conversation: orders, payment history or whatever your team needs at hand.

FINISH.TITLE: You know how to connect tools
FINISH.BODY: Start with a single integration and check it against a real case before you connect the next one.

DATA_IMPORT.NAME: Import data
DATA_IMPORT.DESCRIPTION: Bring contacts and conversations over from another support tool and follow the progress.

CONCEPT.TITLE: Moving without losing history
CONCEPT.BODY: If you are coming from another support tool, you can bring your contacts and their past conversations into this account.

WHERE.TITLE: Settings → Data
WHERE.BODY: Open Settings and go to Data. This is where imports are started and where you review the history of previous ones.

PAGE.TITLE: Import and Export
PAGE.BODY: The header has two tabs. Import is the one you will use today; Export is still on its way and shows up as Coming soon.

NEW.TITLE: Start an import
NEW.BODY: The Import button opens the new import panel. Only one import can run at a time, so wait for the active one to finish.

SOURCES.TITLE: Source and credentials
SOURCES.BODY: Pick the source (Intercom or Freshdesk), name the import, paste the access key and tick what to bring: contacts, conversations or messages.

LIST.TITLE: Recent imports
LIST.BODY: Each row is one import with its source, type, status and how many records came in. Click it to open the detail view.

PROGRESS.TITLE: It runs in the background
PROGRESS.BODY: The import keeps going even if you close the page. The status updates on its own: queued, importing contacts, finalizing.

DETAIL.TITLE: Errors and skipped records
DETAIL.BODY: Inside an import you see the progress, the errors and what was skipped. Both lists download as CSV so you can review them calmly.

FINISH.TITLE: Your history is here
FINISH.BODY: After importing, go through the skipped records and fix what needs fixing before you call the migration done.

AUDIT_LOGS.NAME: Audit logs
AUDIT_LOGS.DESCRIPTION: See who did what in the account and from where, to audit changes and investigate incidents.

CONCEPT.TITLE: Your account's history
CONCEPT.BODY: The audit log keeps who made every important change and when. It is how you find out what happened when something looks off.

WHERE.TITLE: Settings → Audit Logs
WHERE.BODY: Open Settings and go to Audit logs. Only administrators can read it.

PAGE.TITLE: The event list
PAGE.BODY: Events show newest first, with the total count at the top and pagination at the bottom of the table.

ENTRIES.TITLE: What gets recorded
ENTRIES.BODY: Sign-ins and sign-outs, invitations and role changes, inboxes, teams, macros, webhooks and automation rules created or removed.

FILTERS.TITLE: Search and filter
FILTERS.BODY: From the header you filter by event type and date range, and the search box narrows by name or email. Clear the filters when you are done.

IP.TITLE: Time and IP address
IP.BODY: Every line carries the exact time and the IP the action came from. That is the key detail when you investigate a strange sign-in.

USES.TITLE: When to look here
USES.BODY: When a setting disappears, when someone loses access, or when you need evidence for a security review.

FINISH.TITLE: You can audit your account
FINISH.BODY: You do not need to read it daily. Open it with a concrete question and filter by date to get there fast.

SECURITY_SSO.NAME: Security and SSO
SECURITY_SSO.DESCRIPTION: Set up SAML single sign-on so your team signs in with your company credentials.

CONCEPT.TITLE: One key to get in
CONCEPT.BODY: With SSO your team signs in with the company credentials instead of a separate password. Fewer passwords, less risk.

WHERE.TITLE: Settings → Security
WHERE.BODY: Open Settings and go to Security. If SAML sign-in is not enabled on the instance, the page will tell you so.

PAGE.TITLE: SAML SSO
PAGE.BODY: SAML is the standard that connects LuxoInbox to your identity provider: Google Workspace, Microsoft Entra, Okta and the like.

IDENTITY_PROVIDER.TITLE: Details from your provider
IDENTITY_PROVIDER.BODY: You need three values from your provider: the SSO URL, the Identity Provider Entity ID and the signing certificate in PEM format.

SERVICE_PROVIDER.TITLE: Details you copy back
SERVICE_PROVIDER.BODY: The service provider information section holds the ACS URL and the SP Entity ID. Paste them into your IdP configuration.

ATTRIBUTES.TITLE: Attributes you must send
ATTRIBUTES.BODY: Your provider has to send the attributes listed on the page, such as email and name. Sign-in fails without them.

ROLLOUT.TITLE: Test before you announce it
ROLLOUT.BODY: Save with Update SAML Settings and test with one account before telling the team. Keep one administrator on email sign-in.

FINISH.TITLE: Your access is corporate now
FINISH.BODY: With SSO on, removing someone in your provider removes their access here too. That is the real win.

BILLING.NAME: Billing
BILLING.DESCRIPTION: Review your plan, seats and credits, and manage the subscription from the billing portal.

CONCEPT.TITLE: Your plan and your usage
CONCEPT.BODY: This section sums up which plan you are on, how many people it covers and when it renews. It only exists on the cloud version.

WHERE.TITLE: Settings → Billing
WHERE.BODY: Open Settings and go to Billing. It is an administrator-only section.

PAGE.TITLE: The billing page
PAGE.BODY: At the top there is a View Pricing link to compare plans, and below it the cards with your subscription and your usage.

CURRENT_PLAN.TITLE: Current plan and seats
CURRENT_PLAN.BODY: You see your plan, the number of seats you pay for, the renewal date and the currency. One seat equals one active agent.

PORTAL.TITLE: The billing portal
PORTAL.BODY: Go to the billing portal opens your past invoices, lets you change payment details or cancel the subscription.

CREDITS.TITLE: LuxoIA credits
CREDITS.BODY: If you use LuxoIA you get two meters, responses and documents, with this month's usage. You can buy more credits when they run out.

SUPPORT.TITLE: If something looks wrong
SUPPORT.BODY: The Chat with us button opens direct support for charge questions, plan changes or invoices you cannot find.

FINISH.TITLE: You are on top of your subscription
FINISH.BODY: Review the seats every time someone joins or leaves the team: it is the setting that moves your bill the most.

LAUNCHER.ARIA_LABEL: Open the tutorials for this screen
LAUNCHER.TITLE: On this screen

START.NAME: Getting started
START.DESCRIPTION: Find your way around LuxoInbox: the sidebar, search, your profile and your accounts.

CONVERSATIONS.NAME: Conversations
CONVERSATIONS.DESCRIPTION: Reply, filter, organize and close the conversations that reach your team.

CONTACTS.NAME: Contacts and companies
CONTACTS.DESCRIPTION: Keep your records in order: search, segments, imports and company profiles.

CHANNELS.NAME: Channels and inboxes
CHANNELS.DESCRIPTION: Connect WhatsApp, email, social networks and the web chat, then tune each inbox.

TEAM.NAME: Team and permissions
TEAM.DESCRIPTION: Invite agents, build teams and decide what each role is allowed to do.

PRODUCTIVITY.NAME: Productivity and automation
PRODUCTIVITY.DESCRIPTION: Labels, canned responses, macros, automation rules and SLAs that save you time.

AI.NAME: LuxoIA
AI.DESCRIPTION: Set up your AI assistant: FAQs, documents, scenarios and the inboxes it answers in.

CAMPAIGNS.NAME: Campaigns
CAMPAIGNS.DESCRIPTION: Reach out first with live chat, SMS and WhatsApp campaigns.

HELP_CENTER.NAME: Help center
HELP_CENTER.DESCRIPTION: Publish your own knowledge base: portals, articles, categories and languages.

REPORTS.NAME: Reports
REPORTS.DESCRIPTION: Measure your operation: conversations, agents, labels, CSAT and SLAs.

ACCOUNT.NAME: Account, security and integrations
ACCOUNT.DESCRIPTION: Account settings, integrations, webhooks, data imports and security.

CALLS.NAME: Calls
CALLS.DESCRIPTION: Take and place calls from LuxoInbox without leaving the conversation.
